arquivo.titulo: Structural Colour in Bees (Hymenoptera: Anthophila) Is Linked to Climate and Latitude
arquivo.autores: Patricia Henríquez‐Piskulich, Iliana Medina, Andrew F. Hugall, Fabian C. Salgado‐Roa, Katrina J. Rankin, Mark A. Elgar et al.
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Aim Environmental drivers frequently predict global patterns of colour diversity, but whether such patterns depend on the underlying colour mechanisms—pigments or microscopic structures—has scarcely been considered. Structural colour may have different functional properties that result in different associations with environmental variables. Here we test whether the presence of structural colour is linked with environmental variables that reflect potential thermoregulatory and water‐repellent properties. Location Global. arquivo.resumo: Ecosystem services, the benefits people derive from nature, provides a conceptual structure by which to explicitly characterize and protect the coupled human-nature relationships that are central to human well-being, the integrity of ecosystems, and sustainable development. We suggest the ecosystem services concept may complement and broaden the International Commission on Radiological Protection's currently established framework of radiological protection (RP) through intentional reflection on the interconnection between people and their environment. As operationalization of an ecosystem…

arquivo.titulo: A survey of bees (Hymenoptera, Apoidea) in the Bear River Mountains in northern Utah
arquivo.autores: Lindsie M. McCabe, Byron Love, Jonathan Berenguer Uhuad Koch, Skyler J. Burrows, Kelsey K. Graham, Diana Cox-Foster
arquivo.resumo: Bees provide critical pollination services to a diversity of flowering plants, facilitating the function of terrestrial ecosystems and global food production. Here, we present a checklist of bee species collected in conjunction with a larger systematic study in the Bear River Mountains of northern Utah, United States, over the course of three consecutive summers (2020-2022). The survey was conducted on public lands managed by the United States Forest Service. We collected 8,500 bee specimens using pan traps, hand nets and trap nests, representing at least 199 bee species belonging to 33…

arquivo.titulo: Key to long horn bee species of the tribe Eucerini (Hymenoptera, Apoidea, Apidae) occurring in Europe
arquivo.autores: ACHIK DORCHIN, Blandine Rigaut, Denis Michez
arquivo.resumo: Europe hosts some 2180 wild bee species, representing ca 10% of the world bee diversity. The long horn bee tribe Eucerini (Hymenoptera, Apidae) is one of the most charismatic groups in this region, and is particularly diverse in the southern, Euro-Mediterranean region. While identification of most species is difficult, a comprehensive identification tool has largely been missing, but is essential for current monitoring programs. This work presents the first modern comprehensive key to species of the tribe Eucerini in Europe. Keys are provided separately for females and males, including 89 out…

arquivo.titulo: Neither lost nor quite forgotten: tracing 19th and early 20th century bee types in the collections of Oxford and Paris (Hymenoptera, Apoidea)
arquivo.autores: Thomas James Wood
arquivo.resumo: Ni perdus ni tout à fait oubliés: à la recherche des types d'abeilles du XIXe et du début du XXe siècle dans les collections d'Oxford et de Paris (Hymenoptera, Apoidea). Les collections historiques sont un aspect indispensable de l'étude de la biodiversité, mais les types dispersés, perdus ou mal interprétés rendent cette étude difficile. Les efforts déployés pour retrouver des types méconnus d'abeilles décrites par des auteurs français, principalement dans les muséums d'Oxford et de Paris, sont ici présentés. Des lectotypes sont désignés pour les taxons suivants: Anthophora aerizusa Vachal,…

arquivo.titulo: Navigating through the high species diversity of wild bees (Hymenoptera: Apoidea) requires more than identification keys
arquivo.autores: Noé Barbier Chabot, Vincent Carlier, A. Perrard
arquivo.resumo: Abstract In the context of pollinator decline and species-focused conservation measures, the need for data on wild bees continues to grow, and identifying them at a species level has become a crucial issue. This challenge is linked to a lack of naturalist skills, to the difficulty of the group, but also to a lack of tools to train people in this expertise, such as accessible, comprehensive, and up-to-date identification keys. Online multi-access keys are designed to facilitate identification, better illustrate criteria, and enable more fluid updates. These keys require a higher initial…

arquivo.titulo: Why make it easy when you can make it difficult? the nigritus group as example of the current challenges in the traditional taxonomy of the bee genus Hylaeus Fabricius (Apoidea: Colletidae)
arquivo.autores: Romain Le Divelec, Christian Schmid‐Egger, Daniel Benda, Denis Michez, Kobe Janssen, Villu Soon et al.
arquivo.resumo: The genus Hylaeus Fabricius is one of the most diverse and taxonomically challenging bee genera in the Palaearctic region, with a confused taxonomy and unclear supraspecific classification. The nigritus species group, currently assigned to the subgenus Hylaeus, was previously considered to comprise 13 species, primarily distributed across Asia. Despite a recent revision, reliable identification of the group and its constituent species has remained difficult. We present a comprehensive revision of the group based on detailed morphological study combined with DNA barcoding. Our review revealed…

arquivo.titulo: The type specimens of bees (Hymenoptera, Apoidea) deposited in the Zoological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences, St. Petersburg. Contribution X. Family Megachilidae, tribe Anthidiini, species described by V.B. Popov and V.V. Gussakovskij
arquivo.autores: К. S. Ivlev, Yuliа V. Аstаfurovа, Mаxim Yu. Proshchаlykin
arquivo.resumo: The type specimens for names of bee taxa in the tribe Anthidiini, described by Vladimir B. Popov and Vladimir V. Gussakovskij and deposited in the Zoological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences (St. Petersburg), are reviewed. Primary types of 16 taxa (14 described by V. Popov and 2 described by V. Gussakovskij) are illustrated and detailed information is provided. Lectotypes are designated for Anthidium punctatum ssp. zaidamense Popov, 1948 and Anthidium reichardti Gussakovskij, 1930.

arquivo.titulo: A Catalogue of the Bee (Hymenoptera: Apoidea) Flora in Campeche, Mexico
arquivo.autores: Maximiliano Vanoye Eligio, Benito Bernardo Dzib Castillo, Edith González Lazo, Félix Alejandra Luna Medina, Blanca Del Rosario Martín Canché, Juan Manuel Ortega Almeyda et al.
arquivo.resumo: Beekeeping is an activity that generates significant income in various parts of the world. Beekeeping success and production depend largely on the native and exotic flora that surrounds apiaries. The flora influences bee success as well as the nutritional and organoleptic characteristics of honey, so its knowledge is essential for the development and growth of this activity. Therefore, herein we present an updated catalogue listing the flora important to the success of beekeeping in the state of Campeche, Mexico. We reviewed publications available in scientific databases related to the…

arquivo.titulo: Microplastic Occurrence in Foragers of Two Neotropical Bee Species (Apidae: Meliponini) from the Eastern Amazon
arquivo.autores: Bárbara dos Santos Conceição Lopes, María Auxiliadora Pantoja Ferreira, Jéssica Dipold, Niklaus Ursus Wetter, Anderson Zanardi de Freitas, Kamila Leão Leão et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous anthropogenic pollutants that originate from diverse sources and pose a significant threat to both aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Bees are considered active bio-samplers of air quality due to the accumulation of MPs on their bodies. In addition, the ingestion of MPs alters body mass, locomotion, and hemocyte counts without impairing survival. Native bees hold ecological and economic relevance by providing critical ecosystem services through the pollination of numerous wild and cultivated plant species. However, microplastic contamination in…

arquivo.titulo: Diversity of Mites Associated With Stingless Bees (Hymenoptera: Meliponini) in Forest Fragments in Brazil: Empirical Validation of an Efficient and Low‐Cost Sampling Method
arquivo.autores: Éricles Charles da Silva Melo, Milena Emily da Silva Lima, Vinícius Borges da Silva, Airton Torres Carvalho, Simão Dias Vasconcelos
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Despite the importance of understanding mite–bee interactions, standardized and noninvasive methods for sampling mite communities in stingless bee hives remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate a novel, low‐cost sampling technique using a custom‐built suction device, the Portable Mite Aspirator (PMA), for collecting mites from hives of three stingless bee species that were evaluated as healthy: Melipona scutellaris , Melipona subnitida and Scaptotrigona depilis . The research was conducted across two ecosystems, tropical rainforest and dry forest, in northeastern Brazil. The PMA…

arquivo.titulo: Sociality and nesting strategy account for non-random associations between bees and their parasitic dipterans
arquivo.autores: Carlo Polidori, Andrea Ferrari
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Bees (Apoidea: Anthophila) are recorded as common hosts of a diverse array of parasitic Diptera species, but information is widely scattered across the literature, limiting our knowledge of global bee-dipteran association patterns. Here, we retrieved published information on 453 bee-dipteran associations to test the role of life-history traits of hosts and parasites on such patterns. The 13 families and 37 genera of Diptera associated with bees are unevenly distributed across bee families within a specialized and modular network. The family Apidae was the most associated with…

arquivo.titulo: Effectiveness of Pollinator (Anthophila) Sampling Methods across Western Colorado: Implications for Conserving Sensitive Bee Species
arquivo.autores: Francisco Garcia Bulle Bueno, Andrew Draper, Garret K Jolma, Maria Schonewise, Emily Mosswood, Jackie Billotte et al.
arquivo.resumo: El declive global en las poblaciones de abejas ha incrementado la preocupación en torno a su conservación y a los servicios críticos de polinización que proporcionan. Implementar un monitoreo eficaz de su diversidad y tendencias poblacionales depende de métodos de muestreo robustos; no obstante, la eficiencia de dichas metodologías varía entre regiones, hábitats y taxones. El estado de Colorado alberga más de 1000 especies de abejas; sin embargo, las zonas ubicadas al oeste de las Montañas Rocosas han sido escasamente estudiadas en contraste con la región oriental del Front Range. Para…

arquivo.titulo: Diversity of Stingless Bees in the Wasur National Park Area, Yanggandur Village, Merauke Regency, South Papua Province
arquivo.autores: Jefri S embiring, Desmina Hutabarat
arquivo.revista: Journal of Global Innovations in Agricultural Sciences
arquivo.resumo: Stingless bees (Meliponini) are eusocial insects widely distributed across tropical and subtropical regions, including Indonesia. This study aimed to identify the diversity of stingless bee species in Wasur National Park, focusing on their morphological characteristics, mitochondrial DNA variation, daily behavioral patterns, and nest structures. Exploratory surveys were conducted using road sampling and standard transect methods. Species identification was performed through both morphological and molecular approaches, employing mitochondrial Cytochrome Oxidase Subunit I (COI) gene analysis.…

arquivo.titulo: The Missing Branches of the Bee Tree of Life: Addressing Global Darwinian Shortfalls and Their Drivers
arquivo.autores: Felipe Walter Pereira, Matheus Lima Araujo, Anderson Lepeco, Bruno Ferreira Marques, Hugo Bampi, Lucas Jardim et al.
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Aim Estimate the Darwinian shortfall (i.e., the lack of knowledge about phylogenetic relationships) of bees worldwide, as well as identify their drivers. Location Global. Taxon Bees (Hymenoptera, Anthophila). Methods We built phylogenies for over 12,000 bee species, combining the most comprehensive phylogeny and an algorithm with random solutions to insert missing lineages. The Darwinian shortfall was quantified as the Phylogenetic Diversity (PD) deficit, the ratio of inserted branch lengths at the assemblage level. We identified potential ecological and socioeconomic drivers of the…

arquivo.titulo: Mapping the Global Range of Stingless Bees: Insights Into Their Ecological Niches and Environmental Tolerances
arquivo.autores: Pierre Noiset, Leon Marshall, Denise A. Alves, John S. Ascher, Nathalie Cabirol, Luísa G. Carvalheiro et al.
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Aim Stingless bees are the most species‐rich group of eusocial bees, predominantly found in tropical and subtropical regions of the world. However, despite their diversity and importance, significant gaps remain in our understanding of their distribution patterns and the factors driving them, as these aspects have yet to be thoroughly investigated on a global scale. In this study, we aimed to fill this gap by mapping global habitat suitability for stingless bees. Location Global. Taxon Stingless bees (Apidae:Apinae:Meliponini). Method We compiled over half a million spatiotemporal…

arquivo.titulo: Evolution of the α‐Glucosidase Gene Family in Apoidea
arquivo.autores: Jiaqi Li, Wenmi Wang, Yuanyuan Du, JUNXIA JIA, Zhaoming Wei
arquivo.resumo: With more than 20,000 recognized species, the Apoidea is one of the most significant groups of pollinating insects, and their living environment is complex and diverse. The composition of nectar-producing plants for Apoidea varies across different geographical regions, prompting this group to evolve a variety of adaptive traits at the morphological and physiological levels to enhance their survival. The adaptive evolution of digestive enzymes is crucial for efficient nutrient absorption in Apoidea; however, the molecular basis underlying the diversification of bee digestive enzymes remains…

arquivo.titulo: Guarani stingless-bee ethnospecies, traditional management, and perceived threats: a systematic scoping review from the Atlantic Forest
arquivo.autores: Walkiria Aparecida Benites, Laura Jane Gisloti
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Stingless bees (Meliponini) are important Neotropical pollinators but remain underrepresented in Brazilian conservation policy. We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-guided systematic scoping review of published and grey literature on Guarani Mbya and Kaiowá stingless-bee ethnospecies, perceived threats, and traditional management in the Atlantic Forest and associated agrofrontiers. Five studies published between 2005 and 2021 met the inclusion criteria; a multilingual update in July 2026 identified no additional eligible study. We recorded 24 hymenopteran ethnospecies entries, including 22…

arquivo.titulo: Social bees can enhance the persistence of plant–bee interactions during seasonal changes in seasonally dry tropical forests
arquivo.autores: Ana Letícia S. Lima, Cândida Maria Lima Aguiar, Celso Feitosa Martins, Emanuelle L. S. Brito
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Seasonally dry tropical forests (SDTFs) are shaped by strong climatic and resource variability that constrain plant–bee interactions. In the Caatinga biome (Brazil), bees dominate these networks, providing a powerful system to examine how different pollinator groups sustain interactions under pronounced environmental variability. Here, we investigated how social bees influence the seasonal dynamics and structural organization of plant–bee networks in two contrasting Caatinga habitats. We analysed bee‐flower interaction data to test whether social bees, particularly Meliponini, show…

arquivo.titulo: Overcoming the Linnean and Wallacean shortfalls in the northeast of Atlantic Forest: The community of bees (Hymenoptera, Apidae) in a potentially threatened area
arquivo.autores: Silva-DE-Lima JC, Albuquerque AML, Costa PESD, Parizotto DR
arquivo.resumo: The Atlantic Forest is one of the most threatened biomes with a complex evolutive history compounded by subunits and local endemism. Despite that, many taxa, such as bees, is still poorly known in some regions, including several protected areas. These gaps in diversity and distribution represent an impediment in the knowledge of these important pollinators. In this context, faunistic surveys are valuable tools to explore regional diversity, to decrease the Linnean and Wallacean shortfalls. For this, we conducted an inventory of bees in the largest Atlantic Forest remnant north of São…

arquivo.titulo: Chemical Fingerprinting for Authentication and Compositional Characterization of Cocos nucifera Bee Pollen
arquivo.autores: Girliane R. Silva, Déborah Munique Nogueira de Sousa-Fontoura, Rodolfo F. Alves, Francisco de Assis Ribeiro dos Santos, Celso A. Câmara, Lucas H.N. Sousa et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Bee pollen produced by Apis mellifera is formed by the agglutination of floral pollen grains with nectar and bee secretions. Monofloral or dominant bee pollen generally exhibits a more consistent chemical composition and quality. In this study, coconut (Cocos nucifera) bee pollen samples collected monthly for 13 months in Maraú, Bahia, Brazil were comprehensively characterized. Palynological analysis confirmed the predominance of coconut pollen throughout the sampling period. Physicochemical parameters met Brazilian quality standards for bee pollen. Chemical profiling included the…

arquivo.titulo: Field evaluation of pollination efficiency of Asiatic hive bee, Apis cerana under cyantraniliprole and tolfenpyrad treatments in watermelon ecosystem
arquivo.autores: Majid Ikram, Madapuji Rajagopalan Srinivasan, A. Suganthi, Vangili Ramasami Saminathan, J. Auxcilia, Jayakanthan Mannu et al.
arquivo.resumo: Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus (Thunb.) Matsum. & Nakai) is a highly pollinator-dependent crop in which honey bees play a vital role in ensuring successful fruit set and yield. However, insecticide applications during the flowering period may adversely affect honey bee foraging and pollination efficiency. The present study evaluated the pollination efficiency of Apis cerana under cyantraniliprole and tolfenpyrad treatments in the watermelon ecosystem. Pollen and nectar foraging activity declined markedly in insecticide-treated plots on the 1st, 3rd and 5th days after spraying, with the…

arquivo.titulo: Green Façades in the Urban Climate: Microclimatic Performance and Implications as Potential Wild Bee Nesting Sites
arquivo.autores: Melina Wochner, Holger Röseler, Linda Meier, Leonie Katharina Fischer, Pia Krause, Philip Leistner
arquivo.resumo: When designing green façades, parameters such as system type, orientation and solar exposure can directly affect the achievement of the intended objectives, like maximizing cooling potential or promoting biodiversity. Using data from 22 façades in southern Germany, characteristic features and their impact on microclimatic properties were analysed. Considering the microclimate as an important determinant of habitat quality in green façades, the potential for these systems to serve as habitats for wild bees was evaluated. During the summer period a temperature decrease was observed from the…

arquivo.titulo: Hyperoside Derived from Actinidia arguta Bee Pollen Alleviates Zearalenone-Induced Hepatotoxicity and Oxidative Stress in Piglets via the PI3K/AKT Signaling Pathway
arquivo.autores: Nannan Liu, Dongfei You, Yunfei Jiang, Tianyu Han, Guangliang Shi
arquivo.revista: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Zearalenone (ZEA) is a prevalent mycotoxin inducing hepatotoxic effects. Hyperoside (HYP), a flavonoid derived from Actinidia arguta bee pollen, exhibits hepatoprotective properties against ZEA; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying this protection remain incompletely characterized. This study integrated in vivo piglet models, in vitro porcine hepatocytes, network pharmacology, and molecular docking to characterize the molecular targets of HYP. The results demonstrated that HYP significantly attenuated ZEA-induced hepatic lesions and oxidative stress. Computational analyses…

arquivo.titulo: The first annotated checklist of the bees of Colombia reveals an overlooked diversity and areas with major data deficiencies
arquivo.autores: Ruben D. Martín-Rojas, Diego Alejandro Guevara, Juan Diego Maldonado Cepeda, Nicolás David Gutiérrez Rubiano, Danny Vélez, Víctor Hugo González et al.
arquivo.resumo: Background Most existing knowledge about bee biodiversity comes from temperate regions, where diversity is presumed highest—yet substantial data gaps across the tropics confound this pattern. Checklists are critical for documenting species presence, identifying knowledge gaps, and guiding conservation. We present the first comprehensive bee checklist for Colombia, a country in tropical northern South America that serves as a key biogeographic bridge between Central and South America. We hypothesize that Colombia’s complex topography, its position at the intersection of multiple biogeographic…

arquivo.titulo: Plant and bee communities and their interactions are differently influenced by extensive grazing by horses or sheep in the South of France (Causse Méjean)
arquivo.autores: Kerdoncuff Guillaume, Boizet Axelle, Mutillod Clémentine, David Genoud, Lise Ropars, Schatz Bertrand
arquivo.resumo: Pollinators, especially bees, are vital for ecosystem resilience through their role in pollination, yet they are increasingly threatened by the current biodiversity crisis. Large herbivores, by maintaining open ecosystems and facilitating plant dispersal, can contribute positively to increase floral resources with moderate carrying capacity, but the effect of grazing pressure and type on biodiversity remains under investigations, especially in protected areas. In the Cévennes National Park (southern France), the Causses are dry limestone grasslands traditionally grazed by sheep and more…

arquivo.titulo: Six new species of Kelita Sandhouse, 1943 (Hymenoptera: Apoidea: Apidae) from Northern Chile
arquivo.autores: Laurence . Auteur du texte Packer
arquivo.resumo: Six new species of the cleptoparasitic nomadine genus Kelita Sandhouse, 1943 are described from Chile, north of the Tropic of Capricorn, an area where no species of the genus were previously known. All are from the nominate subgenus. The new species are: Kelita cephalalgia sp. nov., K. tignamar sp. nov., K. cocai sp. nov., K. fontis sp. nov., K. keithsheldoni sp. nov. and K. chugchug sp. nov. These are rare bees, known only from one to five specimens despite this area having been surveyed for bees intensively between 1998 and 2017. I diagnose, describe and illustrate each species and provide…

arquivo.titulo: Response of wild bee assemblages and floral resources to management of restored wetlands in central New York
arquivo.autores: Molly Mary Jacobson, Michael L. Schummer, Melissa K. Fierke, Paige Chesshire, Donald J. Leopold
arquivo.resumo: To effectively protect wild bee pollinators and the services they provide, it is critical to understand habitat use patterns across a diversity of cover types. Wetlands are underrepresented in bee surveys, and although wetland restoration produces conservation benefits for birds, how hydrological management influences bee assemblages and availability of floral resources is still poorly known. In this study, actively (full or partial water drawdowns) and passively managed restored wetlands in central New York were surveyed to characterize plant and bee assemblages, June–September 2019 and…

arquivo.titulo: Genomics Reveal Population Crash and Range Contraction in Elusive Fijian Hylaeus Bees
arquivo.autores: Tegan A. Edwards, Damien Esquerré, Nikolas P. Johnston, Stephen D. Galvin, Nikkita L. Maxwell, Francisco Encinas‐Viso et al.
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT The conservation of pollinators is of particular interest due to their keystone role in ecosystem function, but is hindered by systematic geographic and methodological biases such that baseline data are not often readily available. Islands are useful as simplified systems to understand evolutionary processes, are known to host higher bee species richness per unit area than mainland regions, and have disproportionate representation of threatened species. We used low‐lying and canopy sampling paired with mitochondrial and genomic data to assess a recently discovered clade of…

arquivo.titulo: Agricultural Landscapes and Forest Fragments Shape Population Dynamics, Cuticular Lipids and the Conservation of the Masked Bees, Hylaeus communis
arquivo.autores: Sara Olberz, Steven Jansen, Manfred Ayasse, Samuel Boff
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Organic farming has been shown to offer advantages over conventional farming in protecting insect biodiversity, but our overall understanding of its relationship with wild bee population parameters, especially cuticular lipids, remains limited. In the current study, we installed bee hotels at different farming sites in southern Germany and hypothesized that the local farming system (organic vs. conventional), the extent of organic farming, and the extent of forest (percentage of each component in the analyzed landscape) influence the abundance of nests and individuals of small‐bodied…

arquivo.titulo: Sex-specific median lethal dose in bumble bee adults orally and topically exposed to two insecticides and one fungicide
arquivo.autores: Fievet M, Dorio L, Gekière A, Saillard H, Alabiso S, Trapanese L et al.
arquivo.resumo: Wildlife is deeply affected by human activities. Evidence-based evaluation of the main threats is challenging, as it needs to be representative of the diversity of the risk of exposure and the sensitivity of the organisms, specifically for hyperdiverse groups such as insects. While bees are a diverse group of >20,000 species, standardized ecotoxicological data for non-Apis bees species remain limited, resulting potentially in the underestimation of threats that the wild bees are facing. In many cases, pesticide acute data are available for only one exposure route, most often contact median…

arquivo.titulo: Effectiveness of wild bees in the pollination of Citrullus lanatus in the Algerian Sahara
arquivo.autores: Imane Mokrane, Leila Bendifallah, Yasemin Güler
arquivo.resumo: This study was carried out at an experimental site in Laghrousse, province ofBiskra (Algeria), on a Watermelon crop (Citrullus lanatus (Thunb.) Matsum.& Nakai) during the 2024 flowering period. Among the inspected insectgroups, Hemiptera and Coleoptera are considered as visitors; Hymenoptera,Diptera, and Lepidoptera are considered as pollinators of watermelon. Thestatistical analysis showed that Hymenoptera is the most abundant groupand the main pollinators in this crop. arquivo.titulo: Variation in Microbial and Plant Associations Across Wild Bee Families, Functional Groups, and Urban Environments
arquivo.autores: Katherine D. Chau, Trevor J. L. Sless, Phuong Nam Nguyen, Sandra M. Rehan
arquivo.resumo: Bees harbour diverse microbiomes and floral associations which may shift in response to several biological and environmental factors. We examined the diversity of bacterial, fungal, and plant associates (i.e., from foraging or nesting material) across 32 bee species from five families (Apidae, Megachilidae, Halictidae, Colletidae, and Andrenidae) using 16S rRNA, ITS1, and rbcL amplicon sequencing. The included bee species represent multiple axes of variation across functional traits including body size, nesting behaviour, sociality, diet, and native status, and response to urbanization.…

arquivo.titulo: The Future of Native Bees in Australia Under Environmental and Anthropogenic Change
arquivo.autores: Scarlett R. Howard, Kit Stasia Prendergast
arquivo.resumo: The extent and causes of recent regional and global insect declines have been heavily debated, raising important arguments, primarily concerning a lack of knowledge on insect pollinators and their population trajectories. Bees are considered one of the most important groups of pollinators. Anthropogenic activities such as land-clearing, agricultural activities, urbanisation, pollutants, pesticide use, non-native flora and fauna introductions, disruption of natural fire regimes and climate change, among other threats, are having varied impacts on bees. Australia is a biogeographically isolated…

arquivo.titulo: 13. Quality over Quantity: The Oxygen Advantage of Bee Pollen Supplementation.
arquivo.autores: Andrea Aldape, Payton Kinney, Bianca V Trochez Vargas, Brian L Bruner, Cesar Augusto Rosales-Nieto
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Physiological expansions in blood volume can often outpace red blood cell (RBC) production under conditions such as growth, sexual behavior, or nutritional supplementation. This mismatch often causes hemodilution, reducing the ratio of RBCs to plasma and lowering hemoglobin (HGB) concentration. When hemodilution is excessive, systemic oxygen delivery may be compromised due to lower oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood. Measuring anemia’s parameters (Hematocrit [HCT], mean corpuscular volume [MCV], mean corpuscular hemoglobin [MCH], and HGB) can help capture both the quality and…

arquivo.titulo: 18. Mitigating Weaning Stress in Goat Kids: Effects of Bee Pollen Supplementation on Growth Performance and Mortality Rate.
arquivo.autores: Bianca V Trochez Vargas, Diego Villaseñor-Sagrero, Reagan N Sims, Brian L Bruner, Cesar Augusto Rosales-Nieto
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Due to goats' adaptability to different environments and climate conditions, they serve an important role in food security and economic stability. However, at weaning, kids may encounter issues such as weaning stress which can cause impairment in kids’ growth, health, digestive function and even cause death. Therefore, investigating feed additives during the weaning transition that can reduce kid mortality and enhance growth performance is of interest. Bee pollen (BP), a nutrient rich, antioxidant-rich supplement, has the potential to reduce stress in weaned kids, offering…

arquivo.titulo: Enhancing the gastrointestinal resilience of the candidate probiotic yeast Lachancea thermotolerans DiSVA322 using a symbiotic bee pollen-alginate formulation
arquivo.autores: Alice Agarbati, Laura Canonico, Maurizio Ciani, Francesca Comitini
arquivo.resumo: This study aimed to optimize symbiotic formulation to enhance the gastrointestinal resilience of the candidate probiotic yeast Lachancea thermotolerans DiSVA322 using adynamic simulation model, DYGIST system which simulates sequential gastric emptying, fractionary intestinal filling, bile removal via dialysis, and coexistence with stabilized human fecal microbiota. In its free form, the novel strain showed a significant viability drop to 15% at the onset of the iliac phase, decreasing further to 2.3% at its completion. However, even at this final 2.3% viability level, the strain successfully…

arquivo.titulo: Metabolomic Profiling Uncovers Physiological and Parasitological Adaptations to Bee Pollen Supplementation in Goats
arquivo.autores: Argenis Rojas, Lauren K Solice, Reagan N Sims, Brian L Bruner, Adeyemi A. Olanrewaju, Rodolfo C. Cardoso et al.
arquivo.resumo: Parasitic infections compromise livestock health, productivity, and profitability, while rising anthelmintic resistance restricts the effectiveness of conventional parasite control strategies. Bee pollen (BP) contains bioactive compounds with immunomodulatory and antimicrobial potential. This study investigated whether dietary BP supplementation reduces parasite burden and influences liver function, hematological and metabolic profiles, and circulating metabolomic signatures in goats. Thirty crossbred Boer × Spanish does were randomly assigned to either a BP-supplemented group (T-BP; n = 15)…

arquivo.titulo: Inhibitory Mechanism of Bee Venom Against A431 Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma Cells Based on Label-Free Proteomics and Untargeted Metabolomics
arquivo.autores: Yang Ao, Jingjing Li, Wenchao Yang
arquivo.resumo: The incidence of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) has been rising steadily in recent years, yet treatment options for advanced-stage patients remain limited. Bee venom (BV) possesses diverse biological activities including inhibiting tumor cell growth in various tumor models, but its underlying mechanism against cSCC A431 cells remains unclear. This study evaluated the antiproliferative effect of BV on A431 cells using the CCK-8 assay and explored its mechanism of action through label-free proteomics and untargeted metabolomics. BV inhibited A431 cell proliferation in a dose-dependent…

arquivo.titulo: Hidden Amazonian diversity: integrative taxonomy reshapes the Melipona seminigra species complex (Hymenoptera: Apidae: Meliponini)
arquivo.autores: José Augusto dos Santos-Silva, David Silva Nogueira, Izaura Bezerra Francini, Júlio César Carvalho de Oliveira, Rogério Marcos de Oliveira Alves, Gislene Almeida Carvalho-Zilse et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Melipona seminigra is a polytypic complex of stingless bees broadly distributed throughout the Brazilian Amazon and of major ecological and economic importance due to its role in pollination and meliponiculture. Despite the considerable amount of taxonomic information accumulated over time, the identity and boundaries of its constituent forms have remained uncertain. In this study, we conducted an integrative taxonomic assessment based on specimens deposited in three institutional collections, combining traditional morphological analyses with molecular species-delimitation approaches…

arquivo.titulo: Pollination services of managed common eastern bumble bees (Bombus impatiens) in seedless watermelon (Citrullus lanatus)
arquivo.autores: Zeus Mateos‐Fierro, Ashley Leach, Doriana Mierow, John Ternest, Ian Kaplan
arquivo.resumo: Seedless watermelon is a highly pollinator-dependent crop; in consequence, growers stock fields with managed pollinators to ensure high yields. Historically, only western honey bees (Apis mellifera) were used, but, more recently, growers have begun adding common eastern bumble bees (Bombus impatiens) as further insurance. While bumble bees are efficient watermelon pollinators on a per-visit basis, the impacts of field-scale colony supplementation are unknown. arquivo.titulo: Local and landscape drivers of taxonomic, functional, and compositional diversity of wild bees in urban and rural parks in Central Europe
arquivo.autores: Anna Sobieraj‐Betlińska, Piotr Szefer
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Wild bees contribute substantially to biodiversity in agricultural and urban landscapes, yet the relative importance of local habitat conditions, landscape context, and seasonal dynamics in shaping their communities remains insufficiently understood. arquivo.autores: Yang Cao, Xiaoquan Yuan, Jingzheng Luan
arquivo.resumo: The Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm demonstrates strong exploration but converges slowly. To address this, AMRABC_Ts introduces an adaptive dimension modification rate mechanism with two search strategies. Dimension modification rates are chosen according to historical success rates to accelerate…

arquivo.titulo: Bee sting–associated Kounis syndrome with acute aortoiliac occlusion and bilateral lower limb ischemia: a fatal case report
arquivo.autores: Ersin Özer
arquivo.resumo: Hymenoptera stings can trigger anaphylaxis and, in susceptible patients, allergic acute coronary syndrome, known as Kounis syndrome. Although coronary involvement is the best-recognized vascular manifestation, severe anaphylaxis may occasionally be accompanied by major non-coronary arterial events. Acute aortoiliac occlusion in this setting is rarely described and poses an immediate threat to limb viability. A 61-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, active smoking, and known coronary artery disease was referred to our center with anaphylactic shock after multiple bee…

arquivo.titulo: Food resources are more important than nesting resources for explaining wild bee diversity in urban gardens
arquivo.autores: Astrid E. Neumann, Joan Casanelles‐Abella, Felix Conitz, Susan Karlebowski, Stuart Roberts, Julia M. Schmack et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Wild bees are declining worldwide, with urbanisation as one major driver. Urban environments can filter for wild bees with specific functional traits and resource requirements. Nevertheless, cities can support many wild bee species, especially in urban gardens. Yet, we do not know how specific habitat features influence bee species persistence and community composition in gardens, which prevents implementing appropriate conservation measures. We investigated how local and landscape garden features affect the taxonomic and functional diversity of wild bees and their community…

arquivo.titulo: New distribution records of two Lithurgus bee species (Hymenoptera: Megachilidae) from Jammu & Kashmir, India
arquivo.autores: P.M. Osman Javid, Sajad H. Parey
arquivo.resumo: The present study provides new distributional record of Lithurgus bees of the family Megachilidae. Lithurgus albofacialis (Gupta) and Lithurgus atratus (Smith) are new records for Jammu & Kashmir region. Detailed notes on diagnostic features, material examined, and precise locality data are provided. These findings extend the known geographical range of both species in the region and contribute to the understanding of Megachilidae diversity in India. The study underscores the importance of continued faunal surveys for documenting the bee fauna of the Himalayan biodiversity hotspot.

arquivo.titulo: Bumble bees alter diet breadth but maintain pollen macronutrient levels in response to varying floral availability in managed timberlands
arquivo.autores: Rachel A. Zitomer, Priyadarshini Chakrabarti, Andrew R. Moldenke, Lauren N Baugus, Ramesh R. Sagili, James W. Rivers
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Bumble bees ( Bombus spp.) are keystone pollinators in early seral managed conifer plantations, yet little is known about how floral availability influences their foraging behaviour, diet breadth and nutritional intake. In a 2‐year observational study of bumble bee communities in 21 regenerating Douglas‐fir ( Pseudotsuga menziesii ) stands in western Oregon, USA, we quantified relationships between floral availability and diet breadth, resource partitioning and protein:lipid ratio of collected pollen. arquivo.titulo: Diversity of Undergrowth Plants as Food Sources for Kululut Bees (Trigona Spp.) in the Seed Garden of Palangka Raya University
arquivo.autores: Sosilawaty Sosilawaty, Fouad Fauzi

arquivo.resumo: The study seeks to determine the diversity of understory plants and their contribution as food sources for the stingless bees (Trigona spp.) in the Semai Seed Garden and how they might be utilized in agroforestry systems based on biodiversity. arquivo.titulo: Energy-aware hybrid artificial bee colony and reinforcement learning for multi-objective task scheduling in green cloud–fog industrial IoT systems
arquivo.autores: Bo Feng, Jiayi Yang, Yi Liu, Yunyun Yao
arquivo.resumo: Efficient task scheduling in Cloud–Fog computing environments remains a critical challenge in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems due to the conflicting requirements of energy efficiency, latency reduction, and Quality of Service (QoS) assurance. This paper proposes an Energy-Aware Improved Artificial Bee Colony (EA-IABC) algorithm integrated with a Q-learning-based reinforcement learning (RL) module for multi-objective task scheduling in Green IIoT infrastructures. The proposed method enhances the exploration and exploitation capabilities of the standard Artificial Bee Colony (ABC)…

arquivo.titulo: Bees at work: the impact of beekeeping on household agricultural income and the economy in Ethiopia
arquivo.autores: Kelvin Mulungu, Zewdu Abro, Hailemariam Teklewold, Subramanian Sevgan, Menale Kassie
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Managed bees are increasingly used for income generation in Africa; however, their economic impact through pollination services remains underexplored. Using five rounds of survey data from Ethiopia, we estimate the overall and pure external effects of managed bees on household crop income. Results from the preferred econometric model show that households living within a 5-km radius of a beekeeper experience about 12 per cent higher annual gross crop income (about US\$120), while the pure external benefits are slightly lower at 10 per cent. arquivo.autores: E. İşıl Arslan TOPAL, Murat Topal, Erdal Çelik, Erdal Öbek

arquivo.autores: Yang Cao, Hongwei Hu, Yunpeng Jia
arquivo.resumo: Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms can suffer from an imbalance between exploration and exploitation, particularly when the search space becomes large or complex. arquivo.autores: Megan A. Sampognaro, Skyler J. Burrows, Katie Moriarty, Jake P. Verschuyl, Dustin G. Gannon, James W. Rivers
arquivo.resumo: Fuels management is critical for wildfire mitigation, yet our understanding of how this practice influences forest insect pollinators is limited. The DTP is an NP-hard problem that involves constructing a tree in a connected, edge-weighted, undirected graph with the aim of minimizing the total edge cost while ensuring that every vertex is either part of the tree or adjacent to a vertex in the tree. arquivo.autores: Manon Jeschke, Maximilian Stahlsmeier, Olivier J. N. Bertrand, Martin Egelhaaf
arquivo.resumo: Bumblebees navigate complex environments where collisions with obstacles can impair flight performance. While bees possess innate collision avoidance reflexes, they may benefit from learning to identify and avoid high-risk collision areas using environmental cues. arquivo.autores: Nur Amni Khalilah Shaiffullail, Arnida Hani Teh
arquivo.resumo: High moisture in stingless bee honey increases the risk of fermentation, which may adversely affect the quality. arquivo.autores: J. Godard, Maria Cristina Tello-Ramos, T. Andrew Hurly, Andrew B. Barron, Susan D. Healy
arquivo.resumo: Western honey bees, Apis mellifera , and rufous hummingbirds, Selasphorus rufus , are both central-place nectar foragers that navigate between patches of flowers. arquivo.autores: Ujjwal Layek, T. P. S. Bhandari, Joydeb Maji, Prakash Karmakar
arquivo.resumo: Amid growing concerns over the decline of pollinator populations, understanding the diversity of pollinators is essential for optimising crop yields. arquivo.resumo: Abstract Habitat loss and urbanisation create challenging environments for many bee species, but some show a remarkable ability to adapt to urban environments, e.g. by nesting in buildings and foraging in gardens or parks. arquivo.autores: Jatin Kumar Singh, Pradumn Kumar Mourya, Vinod Kumar Dubey, Pankaj Kumar
arquivo.resumo: Bees play a critical role in pollination for various crops and wild plant species, yet their health is threatened by pesticide exposure in landscapes modified by human activities. arquivo.autores: Heng Zhang, Darren F. Ward

arquivo.resumo: Megachilid bees are a diverse lineage of important pollinating insects. arquivo.resumo: This article argues that Paul Murray’s 2023 novel The Bee Sting forges a deep connection between the unsustainability of economic growth and the unsustainability of the nuclear family form. arquivo.titulo: Antimicrobial Trioxacarcin 1,2-Dihydroxyanthraquinones from the Bacterium Streptomyces sp. 127Q Isolated from the Stingless Bee Tetragonula carbonaria
arquivo.autores: Anastasiia Filimonova, Dieter Spiteller
arquivo.resumo: In contrast to honeybees, the Australian stingless bee Tetragonula carbonaria appears to be robust against microbial pathogens. Streptomyces sp. 127Q, isolated from T. carbonaria, inhibited the growth of Lysinibacillus sphaericus, which is the only microorganism reported to affect T. carbonaria. The antimicrobials were purified from Streptomyces sp. 127Q by bioassay-guided isolation using ethyl acetate extraction and Diaion HP20 chromatography, followed by reverse phase HPLC fractionation. The antimicrobial compounds were identified by high-resolution mass spectrometry, UV-Vis-spectroscopy,…

arquivo.titulo: Enzymatic biomarkers reveal sublethal effects of thiamethoxam and fipronil on the stingless bee Melipona scutellaris
arquivo.autores: Lucas Miotelo, Jéssica Freitas Araújo, Osmar Malaspina, Roberta Cornélio Ferreira Nocelli
arquivo.revista: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part C Toxicology & Pharmacology
arquivo.resumo: Bees are key pollinators in natural and agricultural ecosystems, yet they are increasingly affected by the intensive use of pesticides. Although not primary targets of these compounds, bees may be exposed during foraging activities. Thiamethoxam and fipronil are widely used insecticides and have been implicated in pollinator decline. Stingless bees are essential pollinators in Neotropics, making the assessment of pesticide effects on these species particularly important. This study evaluated the sublethal effects of thiamethoxam and fipronil on neural and detoxification-related enzymes in the…

arquivo.titulo: Monitoring of Biofilm Development in Bee Hemolymph Through In-Fiber Interferometers
arquivo.autores: Flavio Esposito, Attena Rashidi, Federica Granata, Carmine Vitagliano, Alessio Avino, Lucia Sansone et al.
arquivo.resumo: This work presents a wavelength-encoded fiber optic interferometric platform for real-time biofilm detection and monitoring. The sensors were realized through a simple and cost-effective fabrication procedure based on overlap fusion splicing of standard single-mode optical fibers. Numerical simulations were conducted to provide design guidelines and achieve high sensitivity. The fabricated devices exhibited a sensitivity to the surrounding medium refractive index (SRI) of approximately 200 nm/RIU in aqueous solutions. The platform was first validated by monitoring Pseudomonas alcaligenes…

arquivo.titulo: Bee pollen as functional food and environmental bioindicator: current evidence and future challenges
arquivo.autores: Luigi Parrotta, Stefano Del Duca
arquivo.revista: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
arquivo.resumo: Bee pollen (BP), a plant-derived product collected by honey bees, is increasingly promoted as a functional food due to its content of proteins, essential amino acids, lipids, vitamins, minerals, and bioactive compounds such as polyphenols and flavonoids. These components underpin its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and immunomodulatory properties. This review outlines the nutritional and nutraceutical features of BP while also addressing environmental influences, safety issues, and allergenic potential. However, BP composition is highly variable, depending on botanical origin,…

arquivo.titulo: A Novel Adaptive Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm for Multi-Objective UFLP Problems
arquivo.autores: Muhammed  Resul Aydin, Mehmet Emin Aydın, Mehmet Emin Aydın, Mehmet Emin Aydın
arquivo.resumo: Facility location decisions directly affect operational costs, service quality, and customer allocation. However, minimising total cost may result in an imbalanced distribution of customers among open facilities, requiring both objectives to be considered simultaneously. This study proposes a novel non-dominated sorting adaptive binary artificial bee colony algorithm with adaptive operator selection, called NSABC, for the bi-objective uncapacitated facility location problem. The first objective minimises facility opening and customer assignment costs, while the second minimises customer…

arquivo.titulo: Bee pathogen sharing and prevalence are linked with flower sharing and taxonomic distance within the bee community
arquivo.autores: Louella Buydens, Alexander Keller, María Alejandra Parreño, Susanne Werle, Michał Filipiak, Clémentine Leroy et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Understanding pathogen sharing within wildlife communities is crucial for conservation. Bees are essential pollinators of wild plants and crops, but their populations are globally declining. Human-induced disturbances may disrupt natural host-pathogen balances, leading to context-dependent virulence. Reduced floral availability could increase pathogen transmission through intensified flower sharing. Here we investigate whether pathogen sharing and prevalence are influenced by plant sharing and mean taxonomic distance between bee species by studying 26 plant-bee and bee-pathogen…

arquivo.titulo: Molecular detection and partial phylogenetic analysis of Deformed Wing Virus and Acute Bee Paralysis Virus in Varroa destructor samples
arquivo.autores: Ali Küçük, Yakup Yıldırım, Özge Sevinç Korkmaz Akar, Abdurrahman Anıl Çağırgan, Ayşegül Usta
arquivo.resumo: Varroa destructor is a significant mite that adversely affects honey bee health, both directly and as a vector for various pathogens. This study aimed to detect Deformed Wing Virus (DWV) and Acute Bee Paralysis Virus (ABPV) by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and to perform sequence and phylogenetic analyses of field isolates obtained from V. destructor samples collected in Burdur, Southwestern Türkiye. Mites were collected from five research regions (Karaçal, Kumluca, Akyaka, Yazıköy, and Çendik), with one apiary selected per region; colonies within each apiary were…

arquivo.titulo: Fostering Colony Growth Post Division: Earthen Pot Hives for Stingless Bees, Tetragonula sp. (Hymenoptera: Apidae)
arquivo.autores: Amala Udayakumar, Venu Hunasikote Shamappa
arquivo.resumo: Stingless bee colony multiplication is vital for expanding agricultural pollination and sustainable honey production, yet it is often constrained by slow natural establishment after division in standard hive systems. This study evaluated the use of red earthen pots as an ideal, natural artificial hive to facilitate the successful division and management of stingless bee colonies. Three different hive types, viz., wooden square hives, red earthen pots, and wooden rectangular hives, were evaluated for the colony establishment after division. Significantly greater percentage of colony…

arquivo.titulo: Floral adaptation and modular trait evolution associated with a shift from bee to hummingbird pollination
arquivo.autores: Pedro Juárez, Kathleen M. Kay
arquivo.resumo: Pollination shifts result in floral divergence, yet how such shifts influence variation and correlation among floral traits is unclear. We examine whether a transition from bee to hummingbird pollination in sister species of Neotropical spiral gingers - Costus kuntzei, with ancestral bee pollination, and Costus wilsonii, with derived hummingbird pollination - drives phenotypic variation, functional integration and morphological modularity. Using field measurements and observations, we assess pollinator assemblages and pollination syndrome divergence by quantifying a suite of floral traits…

arquivo.titulo: Solving Flow-Shop Scheduling Problems with Random Machine Breakdown and Limited Buffer Using a Pigeon-Inspired Hybrid Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm
arquivo.autores: M.K. Marichelvam, Mariappan Geetha
arquivo.resumo: A hybrid algorithm combining two metaheuristics is proposed to solve the flow-shop scheduling problem, aiming to minimise the makespan (Cmax). This approach accounts for random machine failures and limited buffer capacity between machines. Since flow-shop scheduling problems are NP-hard, the metaheuristics could be used to solve them effectively. Researchers proved that the hybridisation of metaheuristics would improve the solution quality. Therefore, this study hybridises the recently developed Pigeon-Inspired Optimisation Algorithm (PIOA) with the artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm. The…

arquivo.titulo: Deforestation Increases Developmental Instability in the Orchid Bee Euglossa imperialis Across Protected Areas of Panama
arquivo.autores: Fernando Moya, Tamara Segovia-Jara, Valeria Tapia, Catalina Aguilar, Jordan Hernandez-Martelo, Laura Milena Pérez et al.
arquivo.resumo: Habitat loss and deforestation are among the main drivers of biodiversity decline in tropical ecosystems, yet their effects on developmental stability remain poorly understood in many insect groups. Orchid bees (Apidae: Euglossini) have been proposed as potential bioindicators of environmental quality due to their close association with forested habitats and sensitivity to habitat disturbance. Here, we evaluated the relationship between forest cover, wing morphology, and developmental stability in the orchid bee Euglossa imperialis across five protected areas of Panama exhibiting different…

arquivo.titulo: Floral resource availability and surrounding land cover influence bumble bee community composition in an agricultural landscape
arquivo.autores: Kelsey N. Shepherd, Anna M. Tucker, Amy L. Toth
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Agricultural intensification and the loss of floral resources are suspected factors in bumble bee declines in North America. Understanding the effects of land use on bumble bee communities at the local and landscape scale is important to support conservation efforts. We surveyed 55 prairie and grassland sites in a highly agricultural landscape in 2023 and 2024. We used a multispecies occupancy model to estimate effects of site characteristics on both community‐level and species‐level occupancy probability. We also evaluated the relationship between species richness and the land cover…

arquivo.titulo: Taxonomic review of the bee genus Caenaugochlora Michener, 1954 (Hymenoptera: Halictidae: Augochlorini) from Mexico
arquivo.autores: Gerardo Quintos-Andrade, Ricardo Ayala, Vicente Hernández-Ortíz, Jorge Mérida‐Rivas, Jorge Valenzuela
arquivo.resumo: Caenaugochlora is a Neotropical genus of metallic bees with 33 species grouped in three subgenera, which are distributed from Mexico to Ecuador. A review of the Mexican species of this genus is presented through the examination of specimens in collections, led to the recognition of 24 species, four of which four are new records for Mexico: Caenaugochlora cyanella Engel, C. leoi Engel, C. macswaini Michener and C. perpectinata (Michener). Thirteen new species are described and illustrated: Caenaugochlora danforthi sp. nov., C. engeli sp. nov., C. esmeray sp. nov., C. floribellator sp. nov., C.…

arquivo.titulo: Adaptive MARL-Assisted Hybrid Bat-Artificial Bee Colony Optimization for Energy-Efficient Clustering and Routing in IoT-Enabled Wireless Sensor Networks
arquivo.autores: H. S. Mohammed, Poria Pirozmand, Sheeraz Memon, Sajad Ghatrehsamani, Sweta Thakur, R. W. Kadel et al.
arquivo.resumo: Energy efficiency remains a major challenge in IoT-enabled wireless sensor networks because sensor nodes operate with limited battery capacity and are often deployed in environments where battery replacement is impractical. Existing clustering and routing protocols frequently optimize cluster-head selection and routing separately, leading to uneven energy consumption, premature node failure, increased routing overhead, and reduced network reliability. This paper proposes an Adaptive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning-Assisted Hybrid Bat-Artificial Bee Colony (MARL-BA-ABC) framework for joint…

arquivo.titulo: Stingless bee honeys: the missing piece in harmonized authenticity and quality standards
arquivo.autores: José M. Álvarez-Suárez, Patricia Vit
arquivo.resumo: Stingless bee honeys are among the most chemically diverse and bioactive honeys yet remain largely excluded from international authenticity standards centered on Apis mellifera . This exclusion may limit equitable market participation and the sustainable valorization of indigenous and culturally embedded meliponiculture systems in tropical regions. We propose a harmonized framework integrating standardized sampling, multi-omic markers, functional authenticity, and inclusive governance.

arquivo.titulo: Physicochemical and Microbiological Profiles of Ethiopian Honey: A Comparative Review of Apis mellifera and Stingless Bee Honey
arquivo.autores: Yesuf Ebrahim, Moges Kibret
arquivo.resumo: This comparative review explores the physicochemical and microbiological profiles of Ethiopian honey produced by A. mellifera and stingless bees, synthesizing data on quality and safety. Across both bee species, key parameters including moisture, reducing sugars, free acidity, pH, and hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) generally conform to National, European Union, and FAO/WHO standards. Distinct profiles emerge between the two types: stingless bee honey exhibits significantly higher moisture content, whereas A. mellifera honey scores superior in total reducing sugars. Crucially, despite honey's…

arquivo.titulo: Evolutionary associations among pollen scopa structure, floral breadth and eusociality in Halictidae (Hymenoptera: Apoidea)
arquivo.autores: Seunghun Jung, Seunghyun Lee, Seunghyun Lee, Minsuk Oh, Minho Lee, Rodrigo Barbosa Gonçalves et al.
arquivo.revista: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
arquivo.resumo: The biological traits associated with the origin of social behaviour remain a fundamental question in evolutionary biology. Among bees, the family Halictidae provides a particularly valuable system for addressing this question, as it represents the only bee family outside Apidae in which eusociality has evolved. Yet, the ecological and morphological factors underlying these transitions remain poorly understood. To investigate the evolutionary relationships among scopa type, floral breadth and eusociality, we conducted a comparative analysis using a multilocus phylogeny reconstructed from 207…

arquivo.autores: Zhengyi Zhang, Fan Yang, Zhihao Zhang, Fugang Liu, Mingsheng Zhuang, Jilian Li
arquivo.resumo: Bacteriophages (phages) are pivotal regulators of microbiome ecology and function, yet their distribution, diversity and ecological roles within the bee gut remain largely unexplored, particularly across diverse bee species and geographic regions. Here, we used a large-scale metagenomic dataset to investigate phage communities associated with seven bee species across China. We recovered 121 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) from 132 bee gut metagenomes, revealing that bee gut phages are dominated by the class Caudoviricetes and include numerous previously uncharacterized viral…

arquivo.titulo: Bee Microbiomes Across Phylogeny and Functional Traits: Examining Host-Cleptoparasite Associations
arquivo.autores: Katherine D. Chau, Trevor J. L. Sless, Phuong Nam Nguyen, Sandra M. Rehan
arquivo.resumo: Studies on microbiomes are essential for understanding the various roles microbes play in the health of bees, yet many wild bees including cleptoparasitic species and their microbiomes continue to be underexplored. To alleviate this gap, we analyzed bacterial and fungal microbiomes of cleptoparasitic species with 16 S rRNA and ITS1 metabarcoding and compared results to the microbiomes of their hosts and other wild bees across families and functional traits. We found that a parasitic lifestyle was associated with a significantly more diverse bacterial microbiome compared to other social or…

arquivo.titulo: Optimizing separation conditions for melittin purification from bee venom using molecular dynamics simulations
arquivo.autores: Azadeh Kordzadeh, S.A. Ahmad Ramazani
arquivo.resumo: Melittin, an anticancer peptide, is the main component of bee venom. However, bee venom also contains phospholipase A2 and hyaluronidase-toxic enzymes that induce inflammatory responses. To facilitate therapeutic applications of melittin, these toxic components must be isolated and removed. This study explored optimal conditions for separating phospholipase A2 and hyaluronidase from bee venom using molecular dynamics simulations. pH = 10 was identified as the optimal condition for melittin separation, as significant conformational changes in melittin were observed at pH = 12. Additionally, a…

arquivo.autores: Sindhu Sheoran, Sally A. Power, Amy‐Marie Gilpin, Sunita Yadav, James M. Cook
arquivo.revista: Journal of Sustainable Agriculture and Environment
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Pollination is crucial to production of most fruits and vegetables but must be managed alongside plant growth and pest control, making it important to understand any trade‐offs between crop management and pollinator health. A key arena is protected cropping, which facilitates crop growth and pest control, but poses challenges for pollination. For example, managed bees in glasshouses may suffer from an unnaturally narrow diet. Co‐flowering plants can be grown alongside crops but may compete for pollinators and thus reduce crop pollination. arquivo.titulo: Local habitat, not landscape diversity, drives richness and reproduction of cavity‐nesting bees and wasps in agricultural landscapes
arquivo.autores: Sara Tassoni, Marit Kinga Kasten, Thomas Hiller, Michael Staab, Frank M. Schurr, Ingo Graß
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Studying insect decline in human‐dominated landscapes, especially in intensively managed agricultural areas, requires understanding its drivers. Studies of cavity‐nesting bees and wasps with trap nests provide information on the number of locally reproducing species and their potential offspring, and how this relates to local resources and landscape diversity. We investigated insect communities across all major habitat types in agricultural landscapes in Germany using a grid‐based design to evenly and proportionally cover the major habitats of our landscapes. arquivo.autores: Ujjwal Layek, Arabinda Samanta, Prakash Karmakar, Nandita Das
arquivo.resumo: Non-Apis bees (including solitary bees) are highly valued for the essential ecosystem services they provide, and their survival largely depends on the availability of floral resources. However, knowledge of the floral pollen sources exploited by non-Apis bees (especially solitary bees and subsocial bees) remains limited. This study aimed to identify the host plants of selected bee species [viz. Amegilla zonata (blue-banded bees), Ceratina binghami (small carpenter bees), Lasioglossum cavernifrons (sweat bees), Megachile disjuncta (leafcutter bees), and Xylocopa fenestrata (carpenter bees)].…

arquivo.autores: Rodica Mărgăoan, Mihaiela Cornea‐Cipcigan, Călina Ciont, Amalia Mesaros, Adriana Cristina Urcan, Răzvan Odocheanu et al.
arquivo.resumo: Bee-collected pollen (BCP) represents a highly heterogeneous apicultural product with the compositional and functional properties strongly influenced by botanical origin. However, the integration of palynological, spectroscopic, and protein-profile data for botanical discrimination and functional characterization remains insufficiently explored. The present study investigated 80 BCP samples collected from the Banat region of Romania, of which 45 representative samples were selected for detailed compositional and chemometric evaluation. Integrated analyses combining palynology, proximate…

arquivo.autores: Z. K. A. Baizal, Gia Septiana Wulandari, Agung Toto Wibowo, Putri Nurika Adila, Saskia Putri Ananda
arquivo.resumo: Developing a recommender system for multi-day tourist route planning that aligns with user preferences presents challenges in optimization. Many previous studies within the scope of Tourist Trip Design Problem (TTDP) have developed systems that recommend multi-day routes by utilizing the analogy of solving the Team Orienteering Problem (TOP). In addition, prior studies have not accommodated the user’s desire to visit a combination of several tourist categories, such as nature, shopping, and culinary, during a multi-day tour. We refer to this problem as a multi-day mixed destination tour.…

arquivo.autores: Leandro Hachuy‐Filho, Caio S. Ballarin, Gerhard Gottsberger, Ilse Silberbauer-Gottsberger, Eduardo A. B. Almeida, Felipe Wanderley Amorim
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Bees play an important role as pollinators, and evidence of global bee population declines has become increasingly common. While most studies of plant-pollinator networks focus on contemporary ecosystems, historical interaction datasets remain rare, particularly in tropical regions. Here, we revisited a historical dataset of plant-bee interactions collected between 1971 and 1975 in a cerrado area from southeastern Brazil that was later converted by land-use change. Using this dataset, we described the structure of a historical plant-bee interaction network and examined how bee…

arquivo.titulo: Understanding Wild Bee Abundance on Marrubium vulgare (Lamiaceae): Biodiversity Patterns in Relation to Phenology, Foraging Time and Sex Ratio
arquivo.autores: Noudjoud Benarfa, Amri Cherine
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Plant–pollinator interactions are fundamental to ecosystem functioning, particularly in semi‐arid environments where floral resources are strongly limited during the summer. Marrubium vulgare L. (Lamiaceae), a widespread wild plant species in Algeria that flowers during the summer period, may therefore represent a key floral resource for wild pollinators. This study investigates the diversity, structure and temporal dynamics of wild bee assemblages associated with M. vulgare in northeastern Algeria. A total of 337 individuals belonging to 41 species, 19 genera and four bee families…

arquivo.autores: Patricia S. Slattery, James B. Dorey, Bruno A. Buzatto, Mark I. Stevens, Michael S. Y. Lee, Michael P. Schwarz

arquivo.autores: Ebru KARADAĞ SARI, Buket Bakιr, Şükran Yediel Aras, Sevda Elis Yιldιz, Arzu Gezer
arquivo.resumo: Bee Bread (BB), a fermented bee product rich in antioxidant compounds, exerts protective effects against diabetes-associated small intestinal damage. This study investigated the effects of BB on small intestinal morphology, mucosal integrity, and antioxidant enzyme activity in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic rats. Forty Wistar albino rats were randomly divided into five groups: control, sham (50 mg/kg sodium citrate), diabetes (DM; 50 mg/kg STZ), BB (100 mg/kg), and Diabetes + Bee Bread (DM+BB). arquivo.resumo: Propolis, a resinous material from various plant sources collected by bees, is known for its diverse bioactive properties – including antioxidant, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory activities. Solid samples were analyzed using attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy and…

arquivo.autores: Skaou A, Aglagane A, Tourbez C, Er‐Rguibi O, Benkhalifa H, Sentil A et al.
arquivo.resumo: Almond trees are economically important and widely cultivated across the Mediterranean. Their yield depends on cross‐pollination by insects, yet their pollinators remain largely unknown, particularly in North Africa. This study investigated the diversity, abundance and pollen affinity of wild bee species in a Moroccan almond orchard. Using sweep netting and pan traps, a total of 813 specimens representing 104 species, 17 genera and 5 families were recorded in the studied orchard. arquivo.autores: Laura J. Jones, Lauren Catherine Ponisio, Shalene Jha
arquivo.revista: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Genetic diversity is critical for species’ persistence and for preserving biodiversity. Regions with extreme elevation gradients, including ‘sky island’ systems, are predicted to restrict gene flow owing to dispersal barriers between high-elevation habitat patches (isolation by resistance, IBR) and the sheer distances between patches (isolation by distance, IBD). arquivo.autores: Arturo Roig‐Alsina

arquivo.resumo: The genus Epeolus Latreille, 1802 is represented in Argentina by E. variolosus (Holmberg, 1886) and three new species: E. argentinicus n. sp., described from Argentina, E. missionicus n. sp., from Argentina and Brazil, and E. parachartergoides n. sp., from Argentina and Paraguay. arquivo.autores: Ngat Thi Tran, Lien Thi Phuong Nguyen, Michael S. Engel
arquivo.resumo: Three species of the genus Gnathonomia Pauly, 2005 (Hymenoptera: Halictidae: Nomiinae) are reported from Vietnam. Two species, Gnathonomia aurata (Bingham, 1897) and G. pieli (Cockerell, 1931) are recorded from Vietnam for the first time, while G. thoracica (Smith, 1875) is the most common species in the country. One species, G. fusciventris Zhang & Niu, 2020, syn. nov., is treated as a junior synonym of G. pieli. An illustrated key to the Vietnamese species of Gnathonomia is presented along with a summary of their distributions.

arquivo.autores: Basavaraj Kadanavar, Saleemali Kannihalli, Kirankumar Rudrappa, Shankargowda B. Gowdar

Among the recorded pollinators, Apis florea emerged as the predominant species, representing 60.22 and 59.33 per cent of the total pollinator abundance during 2023 and 2024. Apis cerana indica (22.39 and…

arquivo.titulo: Bombus terrestris as a suboptimal host for Vairimorpha (Nosema) ceranae: Evidence of limited intracellular development following experimental exposure
arquivo.autores: Raquel de Evan, María Buendía‐Abad, Raquel Martín‐Hernández, Daniel Aguado-López, Clara Jabal‐Uriel, Pilar Garcı́a et al.
arquivo.resumo: Vairimorpha (Nosema) ceranae, a microsporidian parasite that primarily affects honeybees, has caused concern due to its role in compromising bee health. Although the DNA of this microsporidium has been detected in Bombus terrestris and other bumblebees, evidence of active parasite development in these hosts remains limited. Here, we experimentally inoculated B. terrestris workers with V. ceranae spores to investigate whether the parasite can establish intracellular development in this host. arquivo.titulo: When psychedelic discourse meets local narrative: Selective uptake of psychedelic meanings surrounding mad honey in Nepal
arquivo.autores: Sharon R. Sznitman, Surendra Tiwari
arquivo.resumo: AIMS: 'Mad honey' is produced when bees collect nectar from Rhododendron species containing grayanotoxins, naturally occurring diterpenoid toxins that can produce dose-dependent intoxication. It has long been embedded in Nepalese medicinal and ritual practices but has recently become part of global psychedelic discourse. This study examined how globally circulating discourse and local narrative practices interact in shaping meanings of intoxication, using mad honey as a case. More broadly, it assessed the analytical value of distinguishing between discursive circulation and narrative uptake.…

arquivo.titulo: Molecular Docking, Metabolite Profile, In Vitro Antioxidant, Anticholinergic, Antidiabetic, and Antiglaucoma Properties of Royal Jelly
arquivo.autores: Ebubekir İzol, Ülkü Yerebasan, E Esin Kayaoğlu, Münire Turhan, Mustafa Abdullah Yılmaz, Adem Necip et al.
arquivo.resumo: Background/Objectives: Royal jelly is a biologically active bee product with a complex chemical composition and diverse biological properties. This study aimed to comprehensively characterize the phytochemical composition of royal jelly and evaluate its antioxidant capacity, enzyme-inhibitory abilities, and potential molecular interactions with target enzymes. Methods: The phytochemical profile of royal jelly was characterized using liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS). Total phenolic and flavonoid contents were determined spectrophotometrically. Antioxidant activity was…

arquivo.autores: Usia Matsila, Mokgaetji Georginah Mokganya
arquivo.resumo: Pollination-related interactions are essential for maintaining plant reproduction and biodiversity in both natural and human-modified landscapes. Understanding floral visitor assemblages associated with urban and peri-urban vegetation can provide valuable insights into ecological processes that support ecosystem functioning. This study investigated floral visitor diversity, visitation frequency, and floral morphological characteristics of Bauhinia variegata L. in a semi-urban environment at the University of Venda, South Africa. arquivo.autores: BİHTER CEBECİ, Ertürk Bekar, Esra Çapanoğlu, Tuba Esatbeyoglu, Senem Kamiloǧlu
arquivo.revista: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
arquivo.resumo: BACKGROUND: Apicultural products are natural sources of phenolics with significant biological activity, yet limited information exists on the impact of green processing technologies on their stability and bioaccessibility. The present study, for the first time, applied cold plasma (CP) treatment, comprising an emerging non-thermal and environmentally friendly technique, to propolis, bee pollen, bee bread and beeswax, aiming to evaluate its influence on phenolic content and bioaccessibility under simulated gastrointestinal conditions. arquivo.titulo: Tourist perceptions and service design for sustainable community forests
arquivo.autores: Sakol Teeravarunyou, Pongsak Kitirojpan, Kochahem Kamolwit, Pavinee Patanachan
arquivo.revista: Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences Studies
arquivo.resumo: This study investigates tourist perceptions and service design at Suan Pa Ket Nom Klao, a peri-urban community forest in Samut Prakan, Thailand. The research aims to enhance visitor experiences while promoting sustainable tourism, inclusive access to green spaces, and responsible consumption. Guided by User Experience (UX) theory, the Tourist Experience Model, and the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework, the study adopts a multidimensional approach to ecotourism development. Three key objectives were pursued: (1) to evaluate visitors’ perception and activity categorization, (2) to examine…

arquivo.autores: Rahul Dev Verma, Sariyah Akhtar, Jyotshana Saroj, Juhi Sharma, Mohd Mustkim Ansari, Rahul Verma et al.

Three…

arquivo.titulo: Effect of Altitude on Gasoline Combustion Efficiency in Light-Duty Vehicles: Evidence from Andean Corridors (0–4000 m a.s.l.)
arquivo.autores: Paúl Montúfar, Julio Cuisano, Edison Abarca-Pérez, Víctor David Bravo Morocho
arquivo.resumo: Reduced air density at altitude challenges spark-ignition combustion in light-duty vehicles, particularly in Andean countries where fleets operate between sea level and over 4000 m a.s.l. We quantified the effect of altitude on gasoline combustion efficiency and pollutant formation using 94,263 second-by-second records (2021–2025) from ten Euro 2–5 vehicles travelling Andean and coastal corridors in Ecuador (0–4000 m a.s.l.). Emissions were measured with a Brain Bee AGS-688 analyser with pressure compensation; fuel consumption via OBD-II; operational demand via smoothed Vehicle Specific Power…

arquivo.titulo: A conserved miR ‐281‐x is associated with self‐grooming behaviour in Apis cerana
arquivo.autores: Yang Lü, Jiali Liao, Wenyao Ouyang, Chaoguo Chen, Xue Zhao, Yanan Xing et al.
arquivo.resumo: Self-grooming behaviour is a crucial adaptation in honey bees for maintaining individual hygiene and combating parasite infestations. The miRNA-mediated influence on self-grooming behaviour has been recently demonstrated in Apis mellifera but remains largely unexplored in Apis cerana. This study combined behavioural analysis, miRNA sequencing and molecular biology techniques to investigate these mechanisms. We first identified two distinct behavioural phenotypes in A. cerana: strong groomers (CS) and weak groomers (CW). miRNA sequencing of bee brains revealed 12 differentially expressed…

arquivo.titulo: A Memetic-Enhanced Glowworm Swarm Optimization Algorithm with Adaptive Particle Refinement for secure and privacy-aware medical cloud computing
arquivo.autores: Mohd Javed, Himanshu, Snehashree Tripathy, Hitakshi Arora, Tanuj Kochar, Himani Tyagi et al.
arquivo.revista: Journal of Cloud Computing Advances Systems and Applications
arquivo.resumo: Cloud computing has become an influential paradigm for facilitating effective storage, access, and sharing of medical information. Despite its merits, issues related to data security and privacy have remained central limitations to its large-scale adoption in the healthcare industry. In a bid to overcome such challenges, this article suggests a privacy-preserving framework to improve the privacy of healthcare data as well as for securing data sanitization and restoration based on a new hybrid algorithm called Memetic-Enhanced Glowworm Swarm Optimization with Adaptive Particle Refinement…

arquivo.titulo: Modelling pollinator trends using multi‐scale environmental data from the UK Pollinator Monitoring Scheme
arquivo.autores: Claire Carvell, Nick J. B. Isaac, Martin C. Harvey, Robin Hutchinson, Nadine Mitschunas, Christopher Andrews et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Declines in pollinating insects are a cause for concern, yet modelling abundance trends remains challenging and most species are not covered by long‐term standardised monitoring We produce new metrics of change for insect pollinators which incorporate multi‐scale environmental variables into the modelling process to account for various sources of noise and potential bias. Data were generated from three surveys under the UK Pollinator Monitoring Scheme (PoMS) over 5‐ and 6‐year periods, measuring (i) insect abundance and species richness of bees and hoverflies from pan traps across a…

arquivo.titulo: Two New Species of Trichocolletes Cockerell, 1912 From Hiltaba Station, South Australia (Hymenoptera: Colletidae)
arquivo.autores: Remko Leijs, Asaph Whelan, Katja Hogendoorn
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Two bee species in the genus Trichocolletes Cockerell, 1912 (Neopasiphaeinae) are described as new: T. westringiae and T. hiltabanus . Both bee species were found during a survey of Hiltaba Station, SA, a property of the Nature Foundation SA, which was revisited to document phenological differences between bee species. The species are named after the main plant genus they were collected from.

arquivo.titulo: Auxin-induced parthenocarpy as an alternative to pollination of trellised sweet acorn squash grown under protection in fall and early winter
arquivo.autores: Gladys Karungari, Ginat Raphael, Lior Avraham, Sharon Alkalai‐Tuvia, Elazar Fallik, Harry S. Paris et al.
arquivo.resumo: Sweet-fruited acorn squash are a premium-priced vegetable in Israel and are produced under field conditions in the spring and summer. They are also produced from plants grown trellised in screenhouses in the fall, for marketing after storage during the winter months. Ordinarily, in these screenhouses, bumblebees are introduced for pollination when the plants begin to flower. However, viability of pollen and activity of bees are subject to the vagaries of environmental factors. Our objective was to determine if spraying the plants with auxin during flowering to induce parthenocarpic fruit set…
