arquivo.autores: Mohamed Tahoun, Ismail Mohamed, Hassan Al-Mahdi, Mohamed Abdelsabour Fahmy, Hamed Nassar
arquivo.revista: Journal of Umm Al-Qura University for Applied Sciences
arquivo.resumo: Abstract A large body of research has recently focused on minimizing task latency in mobile edge computing (MEC). Researchers in the field have typically posed the minimization exercise as a non-convex optimization problem and solved it either mathematically or metaheuristically, overlooking the fact that neither provides the optimal solution. Specifically, the mathematical paradigm provides a lower bound on the optimal solution, and the metaheuristic paradigm provides an upper bound. The present work is the first, to the best of our knowledge, to explore this fact and quantify the gap…

arquivo.titulo: Analysis of Factors Affecting Costs in Beekeeping Enterprises: The Case of the Western Black Sea
arquivo.autores: Murat POLAT
arquivo.resumo: Sustainability and financial profitability in beekeeping rely heavily on a precise evaluation of unit production costs, hive yield, and regional floral dynamics. This study analyzed the cost structure, economic profitability, and key factors influencing unit honey production costs across 98 beekeeping enterprises in the Western Black Sea subregion of Türkiye. Primary data collected through face-to-face data request forms using Neyman’s stratified random sampling were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Kruskal–Wallis tests, and backward multiple linear regression analysis. arquivo.titulo: Antiviral action of different molecules obtained from invertebrates against avian coronavirus

arquivo.resumo: Abstract Incidences of emerging/re-emerging deadly viral infections have significantly affected human health. For this reason, the search for new products against these agents has become an urgent need. The bioprospecting for bioactive molecules obtained from invertebrates, or their products, sources of research for new antibiotics and antivirals. Honey and propolis obtained from bees and stingless bees demonstrated antimicrobials, anti-inflammatory, antitumor, healing proprieties and several other functions. arquivo.titulo: First record of Aximopsis s.l. (Hymenoptera, Eurytomidae) from China, with description of a new species parasitising the larvae of the coastal pollinator Ceratina smaragdula (Hymenoptera, Apidae)
arquivo.autores: Zixuan Li, Y. Miles Zhang, Zhixuan Liu, Shixiao Luo, Huayan Chen
arquivo.resumo: The genus Aximopsis sensu lato (Hymenoptera, Eurytomidae) is a cosmopolitan group of parasitoid wasps, currently comprising 43 described species. The nodularis species group, which accounts for approximately half of the known species, includes parasitoids of various endophytic insects. arquivo.resumo: The evolutionary origin of the perfume flower syndrome remains unclear. Orchids of the subtribe Catasetinae help elucidate the evolution of this syndrome, but knowledge gaps regarding the pollination biology of Galeandra hinder a full understanding of the process. This study addresses this gap by investigating G. blanchetii, an epiphytic Catasetinae species endemic to Brazil. arquivo.autores: Róger Andrés Hernández-Jiménez, Kevin Espinoza-Requenez, Gerardo Ávalos

Flowers adapted to this syndrome have structures that respond to specific vibration frequencies, releasing pollen onto visiting pollinators. arquivo.autores: Renata Trevizan, Victoria Ferrero, Francismeire Jane Telles, L. Oliveira, Lílian Rodrigues Ferreira de Melo, Felipe Wanderley Amorim et al.

This is particularly important in distylous plants, which have two co-dependent flower morphs with reciprocal positioning of sexual structures (L- and S-morph). Pollen was collected over 17 months at four replicates in the Michelin Ecological Reserve, Northeastern Brazil. Samples were processed using standard acetolysis, and ecological indices were analyzed. arquivo.autores: Mitch Leslie
arquivo.resumo: A little-known arm of the immune system respond to lipids, with a protein called CD1 driving reactions to bee stings, bacteria, and possibly poison ivy.

arquivo.resumo: Propolis, a bee-derived product rich in polyphenols such as flavonoids and phenolic acids, is known for its antibacterial activity. arquivo.autores: Eleni Gemtou
arquivo.resumo: Urban public art increasingly operates as an aesthetic interface through which sociotechnical systems of ecological governance and public legitimacy are made visible or obscured. Drawing on Science and Technology Studies (STS) and Urban Political Ecology (UPE), black-boxing is used here as a diagnostic framework for examining how aesthetic form stabilizes environmental knowledge, political authority, and distinct urban ecological imaginaries through abstraction, participation, spectacle, and infrastructural opacity. arquivo.autores: Marios Alogakos, Ahmed Ghani, Stefan Bitar, Georgia Angeliniades, Konstantinos Manousidis, May Y. Hajeir et al.

arquivo.autores: Maggie Blondeau, Cameron So, Anna Hargreaves

This may pose a particular problem for populations at the edges of species’ ranges, which are often small and isolated and therefore may be less likely to attract pollinators. arquivo.autores: Liuchang Miao, Xinlan Chen, Huoqing Zheng, Stephen John Martin
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Tropilaelaps mercedesae is an ectoparasitic mite of the honey bee Apis dorsata. In the 1950s, T. mercedesae jumped the species barrier from its original host A. dorsata and started causing problems in Apis mellifera colonies in China. Thus, this mite has been part of Chinese beekeeping for over 60 years. Initial reports of collapsing colonies were from three provinces, all outside the range of A. dorsata , indicating the important role of migratory beekeeping in spreading this pest. arquivo.autores: Arjita Choubey, Manoj Kumar Pandey, Ashwani Kumar Dubey, Ãlvaro Rocha

This study presents a reliability-aware framework for speech-only depression severity assessment and its deployment through MindVoice. The distress analysis interview corpus (DAIC), extended distress analysis interview corpus (E-DAIC) and multimodal open dataset for mental disorder analysis (MODMA) are integrated to form a heterogeneous multi-corpus cross-lingual dataset of three classes. The…

arquivo.resumo: Protoporphyrinogen oxidase (PPO) is an established herbicide target. Oxygen-substituted biaryl-pyridine derivatives were designed and synthesized through scaffold optimization. arquivo.autores: Stanka Damyanova, Darina Georgieva, Iliana Kostova, Iliana Nikolova, Vanya Prodanova-Stefanova, Ivelin Dimitrov et al.
arquivo.resumo: Propolis is a natural, accessible, and valuable bee product belonging to the group of so-called bioproducts. Its composition varies significantly depending on a number of factors, resulting in a wide range of data. The aim of this work is to investigate the antimicrobial effect of propolis extract, prepared with 70% ethanol, on packaging paper. Three propolis samples from Bulgaria were used: from the Northeastern region—harvest 1993 and 2023—and from the Central region—harvest 2023. Paper samples from a cellulose blend only and a base paper with improved hydrophobicity from cellulose blends…

arquivo.titulo: A Lightweight Edge Intelligence Method for Student Engagement Pattern Recognition in Blended College English Education
arquivo.autores: Kun Niu, Lei Niu
arquivo.revista: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
arquivo.resumo: In blended College English teaching, student engagement is characterized by cross-stage continuity, multidimensionality, and contextual fluctuation. Traditional questionnaires, teacher observations, and platform statistics are insufficient for continuous and fine-grained identification. To address problems such as the separation of online and offline data, unstable modality quality, and high edge-deployment cost, this paper proposes a lightweight edge intelligence method for student engagement pattern recognition. arquivo.autores: Bonginkosi Allen Thango, Katleho Moloi

arquivo.autores: Pujie Han, Yiheng Liu, Min Huang
arquivo.resumo: In the Interval Job Shop Problem (IJSP), operation processing times are represented by intervals, making machine-sequencing decisions sensitive to temporal uncertainty. arquivo.autores: Jakob Vizjak, Mislav Trbušić, Marko Jesenik
arquivo.resumo: Magnetorheological (MR) fluids are smart materials widely used in applications requiring controllable braking torque and force generation. The optimization of such devices often relies on the finite element method (FEM) combined with a numerical optimization algorithm, incurring high computational cost due to the large number of required evaluations. This study investigates the geometric optimization of a spherical MR actuator using Differential Evolution (DE), Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), and Teaching–Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO). arquivo.autores: Celeste Kock, Corneile Minnaar, Bruce Anderson

arquivo.autores: Mohammad Vahedi Torshizi, Sajad Sabzi, Razieh Pourdarbani, Tahereh seidkhani

Thrincohalictus prognathus (Peréz) is a distinctive species with an elongate face. Although this may suggest a preference for flowers with a long corolla, the species is polylectic and visits a range of plant families including those with flowers which have a short corolla. arquivo.autores: Bidisse Adama, Abba Bilguissou

En s’appuyant sur des entretiens semi-directifs menés au Cameroun avec des utilisateurs des plateformes Yango, OnGo, Gozem et Bee, les résultats indiquent que la confiance des usagers envers ce mode de transport dépend de quatre catégories de facteurs : ceux liés à la plateforme numérique, à l’utilisateur-passager, au conducteur du véhicule, ainsi qu’au bouche-à-oreille électronique.

arquivo.resumo: Obesity is closely associated with metabolic dysfunction, leading to impaired glucose and lipid homeostasis and contributing to the development of metabolic dysfunction-associated liver disease (MASLD). Propolis is a bee-derived natural product rich in bioactive compounds and widely recognized for its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory properties. This study evaluated the effects of Brazilian green propolis, a hydroalcoholic green propolis extract, and a residue-derived extract obtained from the essential oil extraction process on high-fat diet-induced MASLD in male C57BL/6…

arquivo.titulo: Assessing Pollinator Community Recovery in Restored Agroecosystems Using the Recovery Debt Framework
arquivo.autores: Domingo Manfredi Cano, Antonio J. Pérez, Carlos Martínez‐Núñez, Rubén Tarifa, Teresa Salido, Carlos Ruiz et al.
arquivo.resumo: Recovery debt (RD) quantifies the interim deficit of biodiversity and function during the recovery process after disturbance. Unlike typical recovery indices derived from data on experimental-control comparisons, RD further considers the target (reference) biodiversity level, modelling the rate at which it is approached over time. However, the application of the RD approach to active restoration has not been explicitly implemented to date. Here, we extend the RD framework to evaluate active ecological restoration in agricultural systems, defining the onset of recovery as the shift from…

arquivo.titulo: ePosters
arquivo.autores: Marija S. Milić, Vladimir Todorović, Milan Vučetić, Nataša Glišović Milosavljević
arquivo.resumo: Objective: To evaluate the reliability and limitations of most frequently used supervised machine learning models (SMLMs) in predicting 10-year dental implant failure. Materials & Methods: A synthetic dataset containing 10,000 patients' data regarding demographic and clinical patient-related variables, implant-specific variables, as well as risk factors associated with dental implant outcomes, was used. Multiple SMLMs (logistic regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Extra Trees, and multilayer perceptron) were trained, evaluated, and compared. Hyperparameter optimisation was performed…

arquivo.titulo: Reduced Tillage in Organic Farming Increases Both the Potential Services and Disservices Provided by Arable Weed Communities
arquivo.autores: Nina Leclef, Christophe Lacroix, Morgan Abras, Benjamin Dumont, Arnaud Monty
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Arable weeds are a key component of agrobiodiversity, providing both ecosystem services and disservices: while they can reduce crop yields (disservice), they also support higher trophic levels by serving as hosts and providing floral and seed resources that sustain pollinators and natural enemies, alongside additional benefits such as reducing erosion and improving the microclimate (services). Identifying management practices that promote neutral weed communities optimising the trade‐off between their services and disservices, is essential. Organic farming and non‐inversion tillage…

arquivo.titulo: Museum Genomics of an Important Swedish Pollinator Reveals Population Stability Across Time
arquivo.autores: Michael Mitschke, Ellen Karlsson, Jovanka Suess, Ibai Ugarte-Zabaleta, Kalle Tunström, Björn Cederberg et al.
arquivo.resumo: Anthropogenic activity has driven a rapid decline in wild pollinator populations over the last several decades. Understanding the genomic consequences of these declines and their long-term effects requires establishing historical baselines for population diversity. To investigate this, we conducted temporal genomic analyses of a widespread and important pollinator, the common carder bee (Bombus pascuorum). We sequenced 102 historical, dry-pinned museum specimens collected across Sweden during the last 150 years, and analysed them alongside 59 modern individuals. While historical samples…

arquivo.titulo: Enriching streetscape habitat for urban insects: A before–after‐control‐impact study in Melbourne, Australia
arquivo.autores: Paula Bell, Georgia E. Garrard, Kirsten M. Parris
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Residential road verges are an abundant and undervalued green feature in urban environments. As we strive to identify novel spaces for conservation in cities, there are opportunities to use the space afforded by residential road verges for habitat additions to support urban fauna. We implemented a paired before–after‐control‐impact (BACI) experiment to assess the value of habitat gardens on residential road verges for bee, beetle, butterfly and moth biodiversity in Melbourne, Australia. These gardens were designed specifically for the insects known to inhabit the area and included…

arquivo.titulo: The Role of Diptera as Primary Pollinators in Tropical Shallot Agroecosystems
arquivo.autores: Nurindah Nurindah, Dwi Adi Sunarto, Sujak Sujak, Otto Endarto, Encilia Encilia, Awit Suwito et al.
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Dipteran pollinators remain undervalued in tropical agroecosystems despite managed bee declines and climate change. This review establishes Diptera as primary pollinators in tropical shallot ( Allium cepa var. aggregatum Group) True Shallot Seed production. Global surveys document 405 crop‐pollinating Diptera species across 254 genera, dominated by Calliphoridae, Syrphidae, and Muscidae. While temperate regions report dipteran visitors in supplementary roles (40%–65%), tropical systems show functional transformation: Indonesian highland observations reveal that Diptera dominate both…

arquivo.titulo: Exploring the apitherapeutic potential of propolis in laboratory animal models
arquivo.autores: Fahri Emrah Soylu, Karima El-Yagoubi, János Körmendy-Rácz, Ekin Varol, Banu Yucel, Soumaya Touzani et al.
arquivo.resumo: Propolis is a bee-derived resinous product rich in bioactive polyphenols and other secondary metabolites with recognized therapeutic potential. This review examines evidence from laboratory animal models regarding the apitherapeutic effects of propolis, with particular attention to its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antimicrobial, wound-healing, metabolic, hepatoprotective, cardioprotective, antiproliferative, and immunomodulatory activities. These properties have led to widespread experimental investigation of propolis in laboratory animal models. Preclinical studies, mainly conducted in…

arquivo.titulo: Harnessing Amazonian biodiversity for sustainable and circular food systems
arquivo.autores: José M. Álvarez-Suárez, Henrik Balslev
arquivo.resumo: The Amazon Basin’s underused biodiversity can transform fragile food systems into resilient and circular ones. This Perspective explores how Amazonian biodiversity could serve as a foundation for sustainable food-system transitions through circular bioeconomy strategies, biodiversity-based food innovations, and inclusive governance models. Fruits, oilseeds, insects, and stingless bee honeys provide essential nutrients and bioactive compounds while supporting circular value chains with potential to reduce post-harvest losses, restore ecosystems, and diversify diets. Realising this potential…

arquivo.titulo: Unveiling the Diversity of Dipteran Pollinators in the Neotropical Realm
arquivo.autores: Takumasa Kondo, Dorys T. Chirinos, Rossana Castro, Jackeline Gaviria Vega, Jeffrey H. Skevington
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Diptera (true flies) comprise one of the most diverse insect orders; however, they remain understudied in comparison with bees and probably play a far more significant role in pollination than is commonly recognized, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. Although bees are often regarded as the dominant pollinators of agricultural crops, accumulating evidence demonstrates that flies contribute substantially to pollination services across a wide range of ecosystems and crops. This review synthesizes current knowledge on dipteran pollinators of crops in the Neotropical…

arquivo.titulo: Behavior and Chemical Ecology in Phoridae (Diptera): A Systematic Review of Parasitoid-Host Interactions
arquivo.autores: Catarina Silva Correia, Milena Gama Oliveira, Airton Torres Carvalho, Artur Campos Dália Maia
arquivo.resumo: Phorid flies are a highly diverse group that exhibits multiple parasitic strategies involving ants, bees, and other invertebrates. Although comprehensive reviews are limited, most studies emphasize parasitoid-host interactions, especially within Apocephalus, known as "decapitating flies" because their larvae develop inside ant heads. Some species, such as Pseudohypocera kerteszi (Enderlein, 1912), are economically important due to their negative effects on stingless bee colonies. Chemical ecology plays an important role in understanding these interactions, as compounds like cuticular…

arquivo.titulo: Combination of Melittin and Clinacanthus nutans Extract Enhances Antiviral Efficacy Against Dengue Virus Serotype 2 Infection
arquivo.autores: Natthanich Boonsatit, Somluethai Fungfueang, Saruda Thongyim, Yingmanee Tragoolpua, Terd Disayathanoowat, George S. Baillie et al.
arquivo.resumo: Dengue virus (DENV) remains a major global health threat, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions, due to the lack of effective antiviral therapies. In this study, we evaluated a novel combination strategy using melittin, a bee venom-derived antiviral peptide, together with Clinacanthus nutans extract to enhance antiviral efficacy while reducing melittin-associated cytotoxicity against dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2). Cytotoxicity was assessed in Vero cells using a cell viability assay, whereas antiviral activity was evaluated by focus-forming unit (FFU) reduction assay, cell-based…

arquivo.titulo: Comprehensive Assessment of Physicochemical Characteristics, Mineral Content, and Antioxidant Capacity of Malaysian Kelulut and Tualang Honeys
arquivo.autores: Badr Eddin Kharsa, Nor Hafizah Zakaria, Muhammad Ibrahim, Mohd Nur Nasyriq Anuar, Fadzilah Adibah Abdul Majid, Radziah Othman et al.
arquivo.revista: Current Research in Nutrition and Food Science Journal
arquivo.resumo: Honey provides both nutritional and therapeutic benefits, making it important to evaluate its quality to ensure safe and effective consumption. The present work intended to examine the physicochemical properties, mineral composition, and antioxidant capacity of Kelulut and Tualang honeys, obtained from different regions in Malaysia. Kelulut honey was collected from Kedah (KH1) and Kelantan (KH2), whereas wild (TUW) and farmed (TUF) Tualang honey were collected from the state of Pahang, Malaysia. These honeys are unique due to their distinct floral sources, harvesting environments, and bee…

arquivo.titulo: Ferulic acid eicosyl ester enhances cognitive flexibility and modulates arousal-related neural circuits in mice
arquivo.autores: Dana Mayer, Iman Hassan, Firat Taskaya, AFSANA CHOWDHURY, Evelyn Kahl, Thomas Endres et al.
arquivo.resumo: Cognitive deficits are a major contributor to disability in numerous neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders, yet effective pharmacological treatments remain limited. Ferulic acid eicosyl ester (FAE-20), a natural constituent of the plant Rhodiola rosea, has previously been identified as an enhancer of simple forms of Pavlovian conditioning in flies, bees, and mice. Here, we investigated whether FAE-20 has further potential to enhance cognitive flexibility, working memory, or spatial learning in mice, and explored potential neurobiological mechanisms underlying such enhancement.…

arquivo.titulo: Search for neural correlates of object and panorama learning in mushroom body extrinsic neurons of bumblebees
arquivo.autores: Inga Fuchs, Benjamin H. Paffhausen, Randolf Menzel
arquivo.resumo: A laboratory-based setup was developed that allowed us to train bumblebees to a rewarding object (local cue) in the context of a panorama and simultaneously to record extracellularly the neural activity of units interpreted as mushroom body extrinsic neurons (MBENs). This setting simulates conditions flower visiting bees face when foraging excluding the compass related conditions. The bumblebees navigated between the colony and the test/feeding arena on their own motivation, starting from a fully functional colony with a queen. They learned by sucrose reward a specific feeding place marked by…

arquivo.titulo: An ablation analysis of feature selection strategies for machine learning–based breast cancer recurrence prediction
arquivo.autores: Şeyma Aymaz
arquivo.revista: Gümüşhane Üniversitesi Fen Bilimleri Enstitüsü Dergisi
arquivo.resumo: Breast cancer recurrence after treatment remains a critical clinical problem that directly affects patient management and survival outcomes. In this study, a machine learning–based classification framework is proposed to predict breast cancer recurrence risk. Experiments were conducted on the Wisconsin Prognostic Breast Cancer and Recurrent Breast Cancer datasets. During the data preprocessing stage, missing values were imputed, categorical variables were transformed into numerical representations, and all features were standardized using z-score normalization. The class imbalance problem was…

arquivo.titulo: Enterotype signatures of multi-stressor exposure inform conservation strategies for mountain bumblebees of the subgenus Pyrobombus
arquivo.autores: Xin Xu, Ruiqing Cao, Jiu-Hong Dong, Zong‐Xin Ren, Yanhui Zhao, Huanhuan Zhu et al.
arquivo.resumo: Bees often exhibit gut microbiome-defined enterotypes impacting their health and pollination services. Bumblebees, keystone pollinators in montane and agriculture ecosystems, face significant population declines might linked to gut parasites, pathogens, and antibiotic exposure; however, whether their enterotypes reflect these specific stressors remains uncharacterized. Here, we investigate the gut microbiomes of two bumblebee species belonging to the subgenus Pyrobombus, which are commonly infested by the gut parasite Crithidia bombi and other pathogens with samples over four years in…

arquivo.titulo: A knowledge-based intelligent decision support framework integrating symbolic reasoning and swarm intelligence for redundancy allocation
arquivo.autores: Joanna Szkutnik‐Rogoż, Tadeusz Nowicki
arquivo.resumo: Decision-making in complex engineering systems increasingly requires the integration of domain knowledge, operational data, and intelligent optimization techniques. Although redundancy allocation has been widely studied in reliability engineering, existing approaches rarely integrate formal knowledge representation with AI-driven optimization within a unified decision-support framework. This paper proposes a knowledge-driven intelligent decision support framework that integrates structured system knowledge, readiness inference, and AI-based optimization for redundancy allocation in complex…

arquivo.titulo: Interfacial synergistic effects of lignin–titanium dioxide composites in emulsified asphalt and their anti-aging performance
arquivo.autores: Xiufang Wei, Haisheng Wu, Hao Li, Minru Xiang, Shengyuan Liang, Jiangcai Chen et al.
arquivo.resumo: Conventional surfactant-stabilized emulsified asphalt can achieve rapid emulsification by reducing oil-water interfacial tension. However, the interfacial film formed by surfactants has limited mechanical strength, making the emulsion prone to coalescence and demulsification during storage and transportation. In addition, surfactants mainly function during the emulsification stage and provide limited protection against thermo-oxidative and ultraviolet(UV) aging of the evaporative residue after emulsion breaking. In this study, lignin-TiO2 composite particles (LTiO2) were prepared by a…

arquivo.titulo: Genome Characterization of a Novel Bisegmented Positive-Sense RNA Virus Infecting the Bean Flower Thrips (Megalurothrips usitatus) Reveals an Active Antiviral RNAi Response
arquivo.autores: Xitong Zhu, Heng Li, Lin Lin, Jianping Chen, Yiyuan Li, Xiaodi Hu
arquivo.resumo: By combining next-generation sequencing (NGS), reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), and rapid amplification of cDNA ends (RACE) PCR, we sequenced from adult bean flower thrips (Megalurothrips usitatus) the near-complete genome of a previously undescribed virus (related to Anopheline-associated C virus), which we named “Megalurothrips usitatus associated virus 1” (MUaV1). The viral genome comprises two linear, single-stranded, positive-sense RNA segments, designated RNA1 (3658 nt) and RNA2 (2041 nt), which shared 35.75% and 23.74% nucleotide identity with…

arquivo.titulo: Microbiota of Polistine Wasps: A Comparison of Four Species From India
arquivo.autores: Anjali Rana, Deepak Nain, Hanamant Shivalingappa Gadad, Shreyansh, Rhitoban Raychoudhury, Ruchira Sen
arquivo.resumo: Studying the microbiota of closely related species can provide important insights into the essential roles of symbiotic microbes in the physiology of organisms. We have studied the bacterial microbiota of four polistine species (Vespidae: Polistinae), from India, using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing on the Oxford Nanopore platform. Many polistine species have been studied from behavioural, genetic, physiological and ecological perspectives. However, few of them were used for studying their microbiota. A recent study on the microbiota of Polistes wattii revealed that its microbiota is similar to…

arquivo.titulo: Culture-based survey of fungi from decaying Vespa orientalis colonies reveals Beauveria varroae as a virulent and horizontally transmissible entomopathogen
arquivo.autores: Ernesto Ragusa, Karen A. Power, Livio Torta, Marika Lamendola, Giovanni Jesu, Giovanna De Leva et al.
arquivo.resumo: The oriental hornet (Vespa orientalis) is increasingly recognized as a significant pest of honey bees in southern Europe and other dry sub-humid regions, where it causes colony losses, disrupts foraging activity, and may contribute to pathogen circulation among apiaries. Current control measures, based mainly on trapping and nest destruction, are labor-intensive and raise concerns for non-target organisms, highlighting the need for sustainable alternatives. Entomopathogenic fungi represent promising candidates due to their insecticidal activity and potential for horizontal transmission within…

arquivo.titulo: Canopy position and tree size structure the distribution of honeydew‐producing scale insects ( H emiptera: C occoidea) in a temperate hardwood forest
arquivo.autores: Susan Frye, Sandy M. Smith, Sean C. Thomas
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Forest canopies are vertically stratified habitats in which microclimate and host tissue quality vary with height. Scale insects (Hemiptera: Coccoidea) are ecologically important components of temperate forest canopies, producing honeydew exploited by bees, wasps and lepidopterans. The spatial distribution of tree scale insects thus has direct consequences for the availability of these resources but has not been described in North American hardwood forests. We quantified the abundance of three scale insect species and unidentified crawlers across upper‐, middle‐ and lower‐canopy…

arquivo.titulo: N -Acetylcysteine-Conjugated Benzoxazomycins and Hydroxymycotrienin Derivatives from a Hymenoptera-Associated Streptomyces sp. SID10815
arquivo.autores: Won Se Suh, Alexander J. Smith, Allan Artavia‐León, Julian I. Rosati, Craig Matthews, Cameron R. Currie
arquivo.resumo: Abstract As part of our continuing search for antifungal natural products, we investigated the secondary metabolites of Streptomyces sp. SID10815, an actinomycete isolated from a ground-nesting bee-associated environment that exhibited notable antifungal activity in preliminary screenings. Herein, we report the discovery of four new N-acetylcysteine-modified ansamycins (1−4) and three new hydroxymycotrienin analogues (5−7), together with six known ansamycins (8−13), produced by this strain. These metabolites were detected and prioritized through a metabolomics-guided dereplication strategy…

arquivo.titulo: Phylogeography of Bombus huntii (Hymenoptera: Apidae) using whole-genome sequences from natural history collection specimens
arquivo.autores: Brandon Meadows, Jonathan Berenguer Uhuad Koch, Rémy Vandame, Michael G. Branstetter, Ava G McKallip, Jeffrey D. Lozier
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Bumble bees are widespread pollinators, and species often span heterogeneous landscapes with varying environmental complexity. Complex topography, along with historical climate, can shape genetic diversity and act as barriers to gene flow, potentially leading to speciation. Bombus huntii (Greene, 1860) is a bumble bee species featuring a broad geographic range, spanning from the southern portion of Canada, the western United States, to the central portion of Mexico. Prior microsatellite work identified signatures of population structure between the northern portion of B. huntii’s…

arquivo.titulo: 3D-printed integrated device including functional paper components for direct Amitraz determination in beehive matrices
arquivo.autores: D. Paolini, F. Della Pelle, A. Scroccarello, C. Fantilli, C. Merola, M. Amorena et al.
arquivo.resumo: A 3D-printed electroanalytical device (3DD) designed to support the complete analysis of Amitraz (AMZ) is presented. AMZ is a broad-spectrum pesticide widely used to control Varroa destructor in bee colonies. It persists in the environment and in bee products, posing health risks. 3DD functions as a portable laboratory with multiple functional zones connected by microchannels. The device supports direct sampling, automates hydrolysis, and integrates electrochemical measurement. The 3DD body houses a functional rotary valve, into which the untreated sample is inserted. AMZ is converted to…

arquivo.titulo: GPS fix‐loss alone cannot serve as a reliable proxy for nest attendance in burrow‐nesting birds
arquivo.autores: Yachang Cheng, Yuxin Lu, Bing Zhou, Qing Huang, Ting Zou, Jieyu Zhang et al.
arquivo.resumo: GPS fix‐loss is inevitable in biologging studies and is typically treated as random missing data, conventionally excluded or interpolated in subsequent analyses. However, the cause of positioning failure may be linked to behavioural and habitat features; therefore, we tested whether GPS fix‐loss could reveal the nest attendance pattern in the burrow‐nesting Blue‐tailed Bee‐eater Merops philippinus by using GPS‐VHF loggers with onboard light sensors to ground truth. While fix‐loss successfully identified 97.5% of in‐nest events, it resulted in a large number of false positives, that is,…

arquivo.titulo: Stabilizing four-electron zinc-iodine chemistry <i>via</i> glycine hydrochloride additives in eutectic electrolytes
arquivo.autores: Sun Z, Wang Z, Gao J, Xie X, Huang R, Mai R et al.
arquivo.resumo: Zn-I2 batteries are conventionally restricted to the two-electron I2/2I- redox reaction, resulting in a limited voltage window and modest energy density. In this work, we demonstrate that introducing glycine hydrochloride (GH) into a bare eutectic electrolyte (BEE) transforms it into a BEE-GH system that enables reversible four-electron Zn-I2 chemistry. The GH additive modulates the electrolyte coordination environment, suppresses parasitic reactions at the zinc anode, and stabilizes iodine intermediates, thereby broadening the operational voltage window with the high-voltage 2I+/I2 redox…

arquivo.titulo: Hints of self-medication? Pathogen exposure-dependent foraging decisions of bumblebees
arquivo.autores: Kamiel Debeuckelaere, Alejandro Arbeláez García, Tom Wenseleers, Hans Jacquemyn, María I. Pozo
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Self-medication is the selective consumption of compounds that reduce infection and is a widespread form of adaptive plasticity across animals. However, relevant medicinal floral compounds remain poorly tested in bees. Here, we used robotic flowers to test the hypothesis that bumblebees (Bombus terrestris) modify nectar choice after pathogen exposure, focusing on quercetin, a common nectar secondary compound with antimicrobial activity. Colonies were maintained as healthy controls or exposed to the fungus Ascosphaera apis or the bacterium Serratia marcescens. Colonies exposed to A.…

arquivo.titulo: Canopies drive the reassembly of pollinator communities and interaction networks along tropical forest succession
arquivo.autores: Ugo Mendes Diniz, Dennis Böttger, Sabine Fernanda Viteri Lalama, Kilian Frühholz, Maximilian Pitz, Julia Windl et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Vertical stratification is a prominent driver of forest biodiversity. As canopy cover is lost rapidly worldwide, it is crucial to understand the role of stratification in maintaining and restoring key ecological processes during forest succession, such as pollination. Within a well-resolved recovery chronosequence in the northwestern Ecuadorian rainforest, we compiled an extensive database of over 20,000 diurnal and nocturnal pollinators and 2,000 interactions with plants and examined the interacting effects of recovery age and stratification on pollinator community recovery and…

arquivo.titulo: Landscape and pollinator responses to lowland fen peatland rewetting: effects of land management, spatial extent, and configuration in the Upper Rhinluch, Germany
arquivo.autores: Vít Kašpar, Johanna Reger, Martin Wendt, Michael Glemnitz
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Context Large-scale rewetting of lowland fen peatlands is promoted as a nature-based solution for reducing greenhouse gas emissions from agriculture. The resulting changes in land management and vegetation composition may modify landscape structure, with unknown implications for biodiversity and ecosystem services such as pollination. Objectives We examined multiple scenarios representing different land management types (either Phalaris arundinacea -based paludiculture or abandoned rewetted fen), spatial extents, and spatial configurations of rewetting. We assessed how these…

arquivo.titulo: Disappearing Natives, Emerging Invasives: Indigenous Knowledge, Biodiversity Loss, and Climate Resilience in Gandaki Province, Nepal
arquivo.autores: Myrle Ballard, Ranjan Kumar Datta, Som Prasad Niroula, Jebunnessa Chapola
arquivo.resumo: Climate change, deforestation, and chemical-intensive agriculture are rapidly reshaping ecosystems across the Global South, with profound consequences for Indigenous communities. Yet dominant biodiversity and invasive species research often marginalizes Indigenous interpretations and lived experience. This study examines how Gurung Indigenous and Dalit communities in Gandaki Province, Nepal understand shifts in native and invasive species and how these changes affect ecological balance, food security, cultural life, and climate resilience. Using community conversations and Indigenous Elder…

arquivo.titulo: Kelulut Honey Modulates Skeletal Health and Bone-Related Molecular Markers in Rats Fed a High-Carbohydrate and High-Fat Diet
arquivo.autores: Sophia Ogechi Ekeuku, Kumeshini Sukalingam, Mohd Fahami Nur Azlina, Fairus Ahmad, Kok‐Yong Chin, Elvy Suhana Mohd Ramli
arquivo.resumo: Background: High-carbohydrate high-fat (HCHF) diets have been associated with oxidative stress, impaired bone remodelling, and deterioration of skeletal integrity. Kelulut honey (KH), a stingless bee honey rich in antioxidant compounds, has demonstrated protective effects against bone loss; however, its effects on bone density, biomechanical properties, antioxidant status, and bone-related molecular markers remain incompletely understood. (2) Methods: Male Wistar rats were assigned to sham, negative control (NC), or KH-treated groups (200, 400, and 600 mg/kg). The NC and KH groups received an…

arquivo.titulo: Research on Trust Evaluation of Access Devices in Ship Ad Hoc Networks Based on Zero Trust
arquivo.autores: Henan Bu, Bo Liu, Menglong Wu, Zhuwen Yan
arquivo.resumo: In Ship Ad Hoc Networks, the dynamic topology and the frequent access and departure in the open environment make the trusted interaction between nodes a key issue. Traditional trust evaluation models often overlook network dynamics and the comprehensive mining of behavioral and historical data, leading to insufficient evaluation accuracy. To address this, this paper proposes a comprehensive trust evaluation model for access devices in Ship Ad Hoc Networks under a Zero Trust architecture. The model integrates direct trust based on behavioral evidence and indirect trust based on historical…

arquivo.titulo: Tropilaelaps mercedesae: an emerging global threat to apiculture – a comprehensive review
arquivo.autores: Mojtaba Esmaeily, Sunho Kwon, Esmaeil Babaeian, Chuleui Jung
arquivo.resumo: Honey bees ( Apis spp.) are key pollinators in agricultural and natural ecosystems; however, their populations are declining due to multiple interacting stressors and their synergistic effects, including parasitic mites. While Varroa destructor is widely recognized as the primary global driver of colony losses, mites of the genus Tropilaelaps , particularly Tropilaelaps mercedesae , are emerging as a serious and still underestimated threat. Native to Asia and naturally associated with wild hosts such as Apis dorsata , T. mercedesae has successfully transitioned to managed Apis mellifera…

arquivo.titulo: Investigating young children's algorithmic thinking in robot programming activities from embodied cognition perspective
arquivo.autores: Ying Zhang, Gary Wong, Biyao Liang
arquivo.resumo: Educational robots have been increasingly used in early childhood settings to introduce young children to programming and computational thinking (CT). However, less is known about how algorithmic thinking (AT), a core CT skill, develops through children’s embodied interaction with such tangible tools. Using multimodal analysis on approximately 30 hours of video recordings of task-based interviews with five pairs of 5-6-year-old children, this study examines how their bodily actions and interactions with the physical environment shape their AT during Bee-Bot programming activities. The…

arquivo.titulo: Thermal processing alters elemental bioavailability from mealworm flour
arquivo.autores: R. Pavlović, Sofia Bouchebti, Walter Goessler, Miloš Petrović, Slobodan Dolašević, M. Bugarski et al.
arquivo.revista: Journal of Insects as Food and Feed
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Thermal processing ensures the microbial safety of insect-derived feed ingredients but may alter elemental bioavailability through matrix modifications. We investigated the effect of autoclaving on element bioavailability in yellow mealworm ( Tenebrio molitor ) flour using a controlled honey bee ( Apis mellifera ) feeding model. Newly emerged workers received either non-autoclaved mealworm flour for the first 8 days followed by autoclaved flour for the subsequent 10 days, or autoclaved flour throughout the entire 18-day experiment. Whole-body and gut element concentrations were…

arquivo.titulo: A Beehive Fuzzy Number Framework for Modeling Uncertain Honey Production Conditions
arquivo.autores: Neaam H. alfahady, Abdulrahman A. Mahmood
arquivo.revista: International Journal on Advanced Science Engineering and Information Technology
arquivo.resumo: Honey production is influenced by uncertain biological and environmental factors, making deterministic mathematical representation challenging. In the context of Agriculture 4.0 and precision beekeeping, this study presents a fuzzy mathematical framework based on the Beehive Fuzzy Number (BFN) to represent uncertainty in honey-production conditions. The BFN framework uses an ordered membership representation, α-cut analysis, fuzzy arithmetic operations, and centroid-based defuzzification. The proposed framework is applied to three uncertain variables relevant to honey production: queen…

arquivo.titulo: The Beekeeping Sector of Kazakhstan and Contributions to the Pharmaceutical Industry: Promising Flavonoids with the Pharmacokinetic Properties Via the Computational Evaluations
arquivo.autores: Şeyda Kaya, Zeliha Selamoğlu, Sevgi Durna Daştan, Tulkinzhon Gaipov, Taner Daştan, Nurdana Salybekova
arquivo.resumo: Background: Bee products are rich sources of bioactive flavonoids with potential applications in nutraceutical and pharmaceutical research. However, differences in the physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties of individual flavonoids may substantially influence their drug-likeness and bioavailability. This study aimed to characterize the pharmacokinetic, physicochemical, and drug-likeness profiles of four representative flavonoids commonly associated with bee products myricetin, galangin, kaempferol, and quercetin. Methods: pharmacokinetic and drug-likeness analyses were performed using…

arquivo.titulo: The Diversity of Hymenoptera on Pummelo (Citrus maxima (Burm.) Merr.)
arquivo.autores: Caihong Zhang, Xiangzeng Xu, Xiaojiao Zhang, Qinlin Deng, Xue Li, Shide Gao
arquivo.resumo: Hymenoptera play important ecological roles in agroecosystems as parasitoids, predators, and pollinators. arquivo.autores: Nichole M. Cubbage
arquivo.resumo: Varroa destructor Anderson & Trueman, 2000 is widely described as either phoretic or ectoparasitic; however, emerging evidence shows that the mite feeds primarily on honey bee fat body tissue through concealed intersegmental membranes rather than on hemolymph. arquivo.autores: Vivian S. Mulokozi, Francis Moyo, Stella Thadeus Kessy, Elkana Hezron

arquivo.resumo: Probiotic modulation of the nasal microbiome can be achieved through oral administration, which relies on the gut-nose axis and systemic immunomodulation, or direct intranasal instillation, which provides immediate local action. Outros temas de abelhas.resumo: Ecosystem services are critical to human survival; in selected cases, maintaining these services provides a powerful argument for conserving biodiversity. Outros temas de abelhas.resumo: In colony collapse disorder (CCD), honey bee colonies inexplicably lose their workers. CCD has resulted in a loss of 50 to 90% of colonies in beekeeping operations across the United States. The observation that irradiated combs from affected colonies can be repopulated with naive bees suggests that infection may contribute to CCD. Outros temas de abelhas.resumo: Bumble bees (Bombus) are vitally important pollinators of wild plants and agricultural crops worldwide. Fragmentary observations, however, have suggested population declines in several North American species. Outros temas de abelhas.resumo: Dirichlet process (DP) mixture models are the cornerstone of nonparametric Bayesian statistics, and the development of Monte-Carlo Markov chain (MCMC) sampling methods for DP mixtures has enabled the application of nonparametric Bayesian methods to a variety of practical data analysis problems. However, MCMC sampling can be prohibitively slow, and it is important to explore alternatives.
